theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 a^4} - \frac {3 b \left({a x + b}\right)} {a^4} + \frac {b^3} {a^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
Put $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \int \frac 1 a \left({\frac {u - b} a}\right)^3 \frac 1 {u^2} \ \mathrm d u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \int \frac 1 {a^4} \left({u - 3 b + \frac {3 b^2} u - \frac {b^3} {u^2} }\right) \ \mathrm d u$$
multiplying out and simplification
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int u \ \mathrm d u - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \int \mathrm d u + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} u - \frac {b^3} {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {u^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {u^2} {2 a^4} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \int \mathrm d u + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} u - \frac {b^3} {a^4} \frac {-1} u + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {u^2} {2 a^4} - \frac {3 b u} {a^4} + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} u + \frac {b^3} {a^4 u} + C$$
Primitive of Constant
$$= \frac {u^2} {2 a^4} - \frac {3 b u} {a^4} + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \ln \left\vert{u}\right\vert + \frac {b^3} {a^4 u} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 a^4} -  \frac {3 b \left({a x + b}\right)} {a^4} + \frac {b^3} {a^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + C$$
substituting for $u$ and rearranging

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a x + b squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x + b}^2} = \frac 1 {b \paren {a x + b} } + \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \int \left({\frac 1 {b^2 x} - \frac a {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac a {b \left({a x + b}\right)^2} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x - \frac a {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac a {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac a {b^2} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {a x + b}$
$$= \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac a {b^2} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac a b \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\left({a x + b}\right)^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {b \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Difference of Logarithms and rearranging

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a x + b squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x + b}^2} = \frac 1 {b \paren {a x + b} } + \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x + b}^2} = \int \frac {b \rd x} {b x \paren {a x + b}^2}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $b$
$$= \int \frac {\paren {a x + b - a x} \rd x} {b x \paren {a x + b}^2}$$
adding and subtracting $a x$
$$= \frac 1 b \int \frac {\paren {a x + b} \rd x} {x \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac a b \int \frac {x \rd x} {x \paren {a x + b}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 b \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x + b} } - \frac a b \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^2}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 b \paren {\frac 1 b \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } } - \frac a b \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x \paren {a x + b} }$
$$= \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } - \frac a b \paren {-\frac 1 {a \paren {a x + b} } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\paren {a x + b}^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {b \paren {a x + b} } + \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by a x + b squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \frac {-a} {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac 1 {b^2 x} + \frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {a x + b} x}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \int \left({-\frac {2 a} {b^3 x} + \frac 1 {b^2 x^2} + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2} {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= -\frac {2 a} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= -\frac {2 a} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {b^2} \frac {-1} x + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= -\frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {b^2} \frac {-1} x + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 x$
$$= -\frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {b^2 x} + \frac {2 a^2} {a b^3} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {a x + b}$
$$= -\frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {b^2 x} + \frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\left({a x + b}\right)^2}$
$$= \frac {-a} {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac 1 {b^2 x} + \frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {a x + b} x}\right\vert + C$$
Difference of Logarithms and rearranging

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by a x + b squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = - \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 b^4 x^2} + \frac {3 a \left({a x + b}\right)} {b^4 x} - \frac {a^3 x} {b^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \int \left({\frac {3 a^2} {b^4 x} + \frac {-2 a} {b^3 x^2} + \frac 1 {b^2 x^3} + \frac {-3 a^3} {b^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {-a^3} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac {-2 a} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac 1 {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3} + \frac {-3 a^3} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} + \frac {-a^3} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac {-2 a} {b^3} \frac {-1} x + \frac 1 {b^2} \frac {-1} {2 x^2} + \frac {-3 a^3} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} + \frac {-a^3} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac {2 a} {b^3 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^2 x^2} + \frac {-3 a^3} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} + \frac {-a^3} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac {2 a} {b^3 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^2 x^2} + \frac {-3 a^3} {b^4} \frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + \frac {-a^3} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b
$$= \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac {2 a} {b^3 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^2 x^2} + \frac {-3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + \frac {-a^3} {b^3} \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b squared
$$= \frac {2 a} {b^3 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^2 x^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Difference of Logarithms
$$= \frac {2 a} {b^3 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^2 x^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + \frac {3 a^2} {2 b^4} + C$$
C is an arbitrary constant
$$= \frac {4 a b \left({a x + b}\right) x} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} - \frac {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + \frac {2 a^2 b x^2} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + \frac {3 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + C$$
Represent with common denominators
$$= \frac {4 a b \left({a x + b}\right) x - b^2 \left({a x + b}\right) + 2 a^2 b x^2 + 3 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Combine fractions
$$= \frac {4 a^2 b x^2 + 4 a b^2 x - a b^2 x - b^3 + 2 a^2 b x^2 + 3 a^3 x^3 + 3 a^2 b x^2} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Expansion
$$= \frac {6 a \left({a x + b}\right)^2 x - \left({a x + b}\right)^3 - 2 a^3 x^3} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Factorisation
$$= \frac {6 a \left({a x + b}\right)^2 x} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} - \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} - \frac {2 a^3 x^3} {2 b^4 \left({a x + b}\right) x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Split into separate fractions
$$= \frac {3 a \left({a x + b}\right)} {b^4 x} - \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 b^4 x^2} - \frac {a^3 x} {b^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Simplify

title: Primitive of x over a x + b cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$
proof_text:
Put $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \int \frac 1 a \frac {u - b} {a u^3} \ \mathrm d u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {u^2} - \frac b {a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {u^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \frac {-1} {u} - \frac b {a^2} \frac {-1} {2 u^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
substituting for $u$ and rearranging

title: Primitive of x squared over a x + b cubed
theorem_text: $\ds \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {2 b} {a^3 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {b^2} {2 a^3 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac 1 {a^3} \ln \size {a x + b} + C$
proof_text:
Put $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\d u} {\d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \int \frac 1 a \paren {\frac {u - b} a}^2 \frac 1 {u^2} \rd u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \int \frac 1 {a^3} \paren {\frac 1 u - \frac {2 b} {u^2} + \frac {b^2} {u^3} } \rd u$$
Square of Difference, and simplification
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {\d u} u - \frac {2 b} {a^3} \int \frac {\d u} {u^2} + \frac {b^2} {a^3} \int \frac {\d u} {u^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \ln \size u - \frac {2 b} {a^3} \int \frac {\d u} {u^2} + \frac {b^2} {a^3} \int \frac {\d u} {u^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \ln \size u - \frac {2 b} {a^3} \frac {-1} u + \frac {b^2} {a^3} \frac {-1} {2 u^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {2 b} {a^3 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {b^2} {2 a^3 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac 1 {a^3} \ln \size {a x + b} + C$$
substituting for $u$ and rearranging

title: Primitive of x cubed over a x + b cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x^3 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac x {a^3} - \frac {3 b^2} {a^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {b^3} {2 a^4 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \ln \size {a x + b} + C$
proof_text:
Put $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\d u} {\d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int \frac {x^3 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \int \frac 1 a \paren {\frac {u - b} a}^3 \frac 1 {u^3} \rd u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \int \frac 1 {a^4} \paren {1 - \frac {3 b} u + \frac {3 b^2} {u^2} - \frac {b^3} {u^3} } \rd u$$
multiplying out and simplification
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \d u - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} u + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} {u^2} - \frac {b^3} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} {u^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac u {a^4} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} u + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} {u^2} - \frac {b^3} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} {u^3} + C$$
Primitive of Constant
$$= \frac u {a^4} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \int \frac {\d u} u + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \frac {-1} u - \frac {b^3} {a^4} \frac {-1} {2 u^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac u {a^4} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \ln \size u - \frac {3 b^2} {a^4 u} + \frac {b^3} {2 a^4 u^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {a x + b} {a^4} - \frac {3 b^2} {a^4 \paren {a x + b} )} + \frac {b^3} {2 a^4 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \ln \size {a x + b} + C$$
substituting for $u$ and rearranging
$$= \frac x {a^3} + \frac b {a^4} - \frac {3 b^2} {a^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {b^3} {2 a^4 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \ln \size {a x + b} + C$$
separating first term
$$= \frac x {a^3} - \frac {3 b^2} {a^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {b^3} {2 a^4 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \ln \size {a x + b} + C$$
subsuming $\dfrac b {a^4}$ into the arbitrary constant $C$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a x + b cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \int \left({\frac 1 {b^3 x} - \frac a {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac a {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac a {b \left({a x + b}\right)^3} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x - \frac a {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} - \frac a {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac a {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} - \frac a {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac a {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b
$$= \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac a {b^2} \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac a b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b squared
$$= \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac a {b^2} \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac a b \frac {-1} {2 a \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b cubed
$$= \frac 1 {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 b \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
Difference of Logarithms and rearranging
$$= \frac {b} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {b^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
$$= \left({ \frac {a x + b} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} }\right) + \left({ \frac {a^2 x^2 + 2 a b x + b^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {a^2 x^2 + 2 a b x} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} }\right) + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
$$= \frac {a x + b} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {a^2 x^2 + 2 a b x} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
$$= \frac 1 {b^3} - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 b^3} - \frac {a^2 x^2 + 2 a b x} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
$$= - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac {a^2 x^2 + 2 a b x} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$$
$$= - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a b x} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$$
$$= - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a x \left({a x + b}\right)} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {2 a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$$
$$= - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a x} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {2 a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$$
$$= - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$$
$$= \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$$
$$= \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac  x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C$$
$C + \frac 3 {2 b^3}$ is constant

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by a x + b cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-a} {2 b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac 1 {b^3 x} + \frac {3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac {a x + b} x}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \int \left({\frac {-3 a} {b^4 x} + \frac 1 {b^3 x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^3} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac {-3 a} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {-3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b
$$= \frac {-3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + \frac {2 a^2} {b^3} \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b squared
$$= \frac {-3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac {2 a} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {a^2} {b^2} \frac {-1} {2 a \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b cubed
$$= \frac {-3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {b^3} \frac {-1} x + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - \frac {2 a} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac a {2 b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-a} {2 b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac 1 {b^3 x} + \frac {3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac {a x + b} x}\right\vert + C$$
Difference of Logarithms and rearranging

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by a x + b cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {4 a^3 x} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2} + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} + \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C$
proof_text:
A partial fraction expansion of the integrand gives:
$\dfrac 1 {x^3 \paren {a x + b}^3} = \dfrac {6 a^2} {b^5 x} - \dfrac {3 a} {b^4 x^2} + \dfrac 1 {b^3 x^3} - \dfrac {6 a^3} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } - \dfrac {3 a^3} {b^4 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \dfrac {a^3} {b^3 \paren {a x + b}^3}$
From Linear Combination of Integrals it follows that the expression can be rendered as:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \int \frac {\d x} x - \frac {3 a} {b^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2} + \frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\d x} {x^3} - \frac {6 a^3} {b^5} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b} } - \frac {3 a^3} {b^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {a^3} {b^3} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^3}$
This can be integrated termwise as follows (ignoring for now the arbitrary constant):
$$\frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \int \frac {\d x} x = \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size x$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$-\frac {3 a} {b^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2} = \frac {3 a} {b^4 x}$$
Primitive of Power
$$\frac 1 {b^3} \int \frac {\d x} {x^3} = -\frac 1 {2 b^3 x^2}$$
Primitive of Power
$$-\frac {6 a^3} {b^5} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b} } = -\frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {a x + b}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {a x + b}$
$$- \frac {3 a^3} {b^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^2} = \frac {3 a^3} {b^4 a \paren {a x + b} }$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\paren {a x + b}^2}$
$$-\frac {a^3} {b^3} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {a^2} {2 b^3 \paren {a x + b}^2}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\paren {a x + b}^3}$
The terms with the logarithm can be combined thus:
$$\frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size x - \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {a x + b} = \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} }$$
Difference of Logarithms
and so the solution to the integral can be expressed as:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {3 a} {b^4 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^3 x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {a^2} {2 b^3 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C$$
While this would usually be considered as an acceptable form to leave such an expression, there is some way to go to obtain the result requested.
So, placing the non-logarithmic terms over a common denominator and rearranging, with a view to our destination:
$$\frac {3 a} {b^4 x} - \frac 1 {2 b^3 x^2} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {a^2} {2 b^3 \paren {a x + b}^2}$$
$$= \frac {6 a x \paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^4 x^2 \\paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {b \paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^4 x^2 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {6 a^2 x^2 \paren {a x + b} } {2 b^4 x^2 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {a^2 b x^2} {2 b^4 x^2 \paren {a x + b}^2}$$
$$= \frac {12 a^3 x^3 + 18 a^2 b x^2 + 4 a b^2 x - b^3} {2 b^4 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^4 + 16 a^3 b x^3 + 24 a^2 b^2 x^2 + 8 a b^3 x} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} - \frac {a^4 x^4 + 4 a^3 b x^3 + 6 a^2 b^2 x^2 + 4 a b^3 x + b^4} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^4 + 16 a^3 b x^3 + 24 a^2 b^2 x^2 + 8 a b^3 x} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^4} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^4 + 16 a^3 b x^3 + 24 a^2 b^2 x^2 + 8 a b^3 x} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {16 a^3 b x^3 + 24 a^2 b^2 x^2 + 8 a b^3 x} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {8 a^3 b x^3 + 8 a^2 b^2 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} + \frac {8 a^3 b x^3 + 16 a^2 b^2 x^2 + 8 a b^3 x} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {8 a^2 b x^2 \paren {a x + b} } {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} + \frac {8 a b x \paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2 x^2} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {4 a^2} {b^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {4 a^2 b} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {4 a^2 \paren {a x + b} } {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {4 a^3 x} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
$$= \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac {4 a^2} {b^5} - \frac {4 a^3 x} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2}$$
Thus the full solution to the integral can be assembled as follows, where $\dfrac {4 a^2} {b^5}$ is subsumed into the arbitrary constant:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {4 a^3 x} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2} + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} + \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C$$

title: Primitive of x by Power of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int x \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 2} } {\left({n + 2}\right) a^2} - \frac {b \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) a^2} + C$
proof_text:
Let $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int x \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac 1 a \int \frac {u - b} a u^n \ \mathrm d u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int u^{n+1} \ \mathrm d u - \frac b {a^2} \int u^n \ \mathrm d u$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \frac {u^{n+2} } {n + 2} - \frac b {a^2} \frac {u^{n+1} } {n + 1} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 2} } {\left({n + 2}\right) a^2} - \frac {b \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) a^2} + C$$
substituting for $u$

title: Primitive of x squared by Power of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 3} } {\left({n + 3}\right) a^3} - \frac {2 b \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 2} } {\left({n + 2}\right) a^3} + \frac {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) a^3} + C$
proof_text:
Let $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int x \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \int \frac 1 a \left({\frac {u - b} a}\right)^2 u^n \ \mathrm d u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \int \frac 1 {a^3} \left({u^{n + 2} - 2 b u^{n + 1} + b^2 u^n}\right) \ \mathrm d u$$
Square of Difference and multiplying out
$$= \frac 1 {a^3}  \int u^{n+3} \ \mathrm d u - \frac {2 b} {a^3} \int u^{n + 1} \ \mathrm d u + \frac {b^2} {a^3} \int u^n \ \mathrm d u$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \frac {u^{n+3} } {n + 3} - \frac {2 b} {a^3} \frac {u^{n+2} } {n + 2} + \frac {b^2} {a^3} \frac {u^{n+1} } {n + 1} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 3} } {\left({n + 3}\right) a^3} - \frac {2 b \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 2} } {\left({n + 2}\right) a^3} + \frac {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) a^3} + C$$
substituting for $u$

title: Primitive of x over a x + b cubed/Proof 1
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$
proof_text:
Put $u = a x + b$.
Then:
$$x = \frac {u - b} a$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = \frac 1 a$$
Then:
$$\int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \int \frac 1 a \frac {u - b} {a u^3} \ \mathrm d u$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {u^2} - \frac b {a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {u^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \frac {-1} {u} - \frac b {a^2} \frac {-1} {2 u^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C$$
substituting for $u$ and rearranging

title: Distance from Subset to Element
theorem_text:
Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space.
Let $S \subseteq M$ be a subset of $M$.
Let $s \in S$.
Then:
$\map d {s, S} = 0$
where $\map d {s, S}$ denotes the distance between $s$ and $S$.
proof_text:
By Distance between Element and Subset is Nonnegative:
$\map d {s, S} \ge 0$
Also, because:
$\map d {s, S} = 0$
and $s \in S$, it follows that:
$\map d {s, S} \le 0$
Hence the result.

title: Distance from Subset to Supremum
theorem_text:
Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers.
Suppose that the supremum $\sup S$ of $S$ exists.
Then:
$\map d {\sup S, S} = 0$
where $\map d {\sup S, S}$ is the distance between $\sup S$ and $S$.
proof_text:
By Distance between Element and Subset is Nonnegative:
$\map d {\sup S, S} \ge 0$
By definition of supremum:
$\forall \epsilon > 0: \exists s \in S: \map d {\sup S, s} < \epsilon$
meaning that, by nature of the infimum and the definition of $\map d {\sup S, S}$:
$\forall \epsilon > 0: \map d {\sup S, S} < \epsilon$
Together, these two observations lead to the conclusion that:
$\map d {\sup S, S} = 0$
as desired.

title: Distance between Element and Subset is Nonnegative
theorem_text:
Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space.
Let $x \in M$ and $S \subseteq M$.
Then:
$\map d {x, S} \ge 0$
where $\map d {x, S}$ is the distance between $x$ and $S$.
proof_text:
By definition of the distance between $x$ and $S$:
$\map d {x, S} = \displaystyle \inf_{s \mathop \in S} \map d {x, s}$
From the metric space axioms:
$\forall s \in M: \map d {x, s} \ge 0$
Hence by the nature of the infimum:
$\map d {x, S} \ge 0$
as desired.

title: Distance from Subset to Infimum
theorem_text:
Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers.
Suppose that the infimum $\inf S$ of $S$ exists.
Then:
$\map d {\inf S, S} = 0$
where $\map d {\inf S, S}$ is the distance between $\inf S$ and $S$.
proof_text:
By Distance between Element and Subset is Nonnegative:
$\map d {\inf S, S} \ge 0$
By definition of infimum:
$\forall \epsilon > 0: \exists s \in S: \map d {\inf S, s} < \epsilon$
meaning that, by nature of the infimum and the definition of $\map d {\inf S, S}$:
$\forall \epsilon > 0: \map d {\inf S, S} < \epsilon$
Together, these two observations lead to the conclusion that:
$\map d {\inf S, S} = 0$
as desired.

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \sqrt{a x + b} } = -\frac {\sqrt{a x + b} } {b x} - \frac a {2 b} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \sqrt{a x + b} }$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Increment of Power of $x$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m+1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({m + 1}\right) b} - \frac {\left({m + n + 2}\right) a} {\left({m + 1}\right) b} \int x^{m + 1} \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x$
Setting $m = -2$ and $n = -\dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \sqrt{a x + b} } = \int x^{-2} \left({a x + b}\right)^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{1/2} } {\left({-1}\right) b} - \frac {\left({-1/2}\right) a} {\left({-1}\right) b} \int x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= -\frac {\sqrt{a x + b} } {b x} - \frac a {2 b} \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt{a x + b} }$$

title: Primitive of Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \sqrt{a x + b} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {2 \sqrt{\left({a x + b}\right)^3} } {3 a}$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Decrement of Power of $a x + b$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^n} {m + n + 1} + \frac {n b} {m + n + 1} \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^{n - 1} \rd x$
Putting $m = -1$ and $n = \dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } x \rd x = \int x^{-1} \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^0 \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {\frac 1 2} + \frac {\frac 1 2 b} {\frac 1 2} \int x^{-1} \paren {a x + b}^{- 1/2} \rd x$$
$$= 2 \sqrt {a x + b} + b \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Root of a x + b over x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } x \rd x = 2 \sqrt {a x + b} + b \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt{a x + b} }$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Decrement of Power of $a x + b$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^n} {m + n + 1} + \frac {n b} {m + n + 1} \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^{n - 1} \rd x$
Putting $m = -1$ and $n = \dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } x \rd x = \int x^{-1} \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^0 \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {\frac 1 2} + \frac {\frac 1 2 b} {\frac 1 2} \int x^{-1} \paren {a x + b}^{- 1/2} \rd x$$
$$= 2 \sqrt {a x + b} + b \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Root of a x + b over x squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } {x^2} \rd x = -\frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } x + \frac a 2 \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x + b} }$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Decrement of Power of $a x + b$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^n} {m + n + 1} + \frac {n b} {m + n + 1} \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^{n - 1} \rd x$
Putting $m = -2$ and $n = \dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } {x^2} \rd x = \int x^{-2} \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^{-1} \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {-2 + \frac 1 2 + 1} + \frac {\frac 1 2 b} {-2 + \frac 1 2 + 1} \int x^{-2} \paren {a x + b}^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {-2 \sqrt {a x + b} } x - b \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-2 \sqrt {a x + b} } x - b \paren {-\frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } {b x} - \frac a {2 b} \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x + b} } }$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by Root of a x + b
$$= \frac {-2 \sqrt {a x + b} } x + \frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } x + \frac a 2 \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
multiplying out
$$= -\frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } x + \frac a 2 \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Power of x over Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\ds \int \frac {x^m} {\sqrt{a x + b} } \rd x = \frac {2 x^m \sqrt{a x + b} } {\paren {2 m + 1} a} - \frac {2 m b} {\paren {2 m + 1} a} \int \frac {x^{m - 1} } {\sqrt{a x + b} } \rd x$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Decrement of Power of $x$:
$\ds \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {x^m \paren {a x + b}^{n + 1} } {\paren {m + n + 1} a} - \frac {m b} {\paren {m + n + 1} a} \int x^{m - 1} \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x$
Putting $n = -\dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \frac {x^m} {\sqrt {a x + b} } \rd x = \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^m \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {\paren {m - \frac 1 2 + 1} a} - \frac {m b} {\paren {m - \frac 1 2 + 1} a} \int x^{m - 1} \paren {a x + b}^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^m \sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {m + \frac 1 2} a} - \frac {m b} {\paren {m + \frac 1 2} a} \int \frac {x^{m - 1} } {\sqrt {a x + b} } \rd x$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {2 x^m \sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {2 m + 1} a} - \frac {2 m b} {\paren {2 m + 1} a} \int \frac {x^{m - 1} } {\sqrt {a x + b} } \rd x$$
multiplying top and bottom by $2$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Power of x by Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^m \sqrt {a x + b} } = -\frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {m - 1} b x^{m - 1} } - \frac {\paren {2 m - 3} a} {\paren {2 m - 2} b} \int \frac {\d x} {x^{m - 1} \sqrt {a x + b} }$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Increment of Power of $x$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^{n + 1} } {\paren {m + 1} b} - \frac {\paren {m + n + 2} a} {\paren {m + 1} b} \int x^{m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x$
Putting $n := -\dfrac 1 2$ and $m := -m$:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^m \sqrt{a x + b} } = \int x^{-m} \paren {a x + b}^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {x^{-m+1} \paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {\paren {-m + 1} b} - \frac {\paren {-m - \frac 1 2 + 2} a} {\paren {-m + 1} b} \int x^{-m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^{-1/2} \rd x$$
$$= -\frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {m - 1} b x^{m - 1} } - \frac {\paren {m - \frac 3 2} a} {\paren {m - 1} b} \int \frac {\d x} {x^{m - 1} \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
simplifying
$$= -\frac {\sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {m - 1} b x^{m - 1} } - \frac {\paren {2 m - 3} a} {\paren {2 m - 2} b} \int \frac {\d x} {x^{m - 1} \sqrt {a x + b} }$$
multiplying top and bottom by $2$

title: Primitive of Power of Root of a x + b over x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^m} x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {2 \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^m } m + b \int \frac {\left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^{m - 2} } x \ \mathrm d x$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Decrement of Power of $a x + b$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {x^{m+1} \left({a x + b}\right)^n} {m + n + 1} + \frac {n b} {m + n + 1} \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^{n - 1} \ \mathrm d x$
Putting $n := \dfrac m 2$ and $m := -1$:
$$\int \frac {\left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^m} x \ \mathrm d x = \int x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{m/2} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= \frac {x^0 \left({a x + b}\right)^{m/2} } {-1 + \frac m 2 + 1} + \frac {\left({\frac m 2}\right) b} {-1 + \frac m 2 + 1} \int x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{m/2 - 1} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= \frac {2 \left({a x + b}\right)^{m/2} } m + b \int x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{\left({m - 2}\right)/2} \ \mathrm d x$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {2 \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^m } m + b \int \frac {\left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^{m - 2} } x \ \mathrm d x$$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^m} = \frac 2 {\left({m - 2}\right) b \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^{m - 2} }  + \frac 1 b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^{m - 2} }$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $x$ by Power of $a x + b$: Increment of Power of $a x + b$:
$\displaystyle \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {-x^{m+1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) b} + \frac {m + n + 2} {\left({n + 1}\right) b} \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} \ \mathrm d x$
Putting $n := -\dfrac m 2$ and $m := -1$:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^m} = \int x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{-m/2}$$
$$= \frac {-x^0 \left({a x + b}\right)^{-m/2 + 1} } {\left({- \frac m 2 + 1}\right) b} + \frac {-1 - \frac m 2 + 2} {\left({- \frac m 2 + 1}\right) b} \int x^{-1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{- m/2 + 1} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= \frac 2 {\left({m - 2}\right) b \left({a x + b}\right)^{\left({m - 2}\right)/2} } - \frac 1 b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({a x + b}\right)^{\left({m - 2}\right) / 2} }$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 2 {\left({m - 2}\right) b \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^{m - 2} }  + \frac 1 b \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({\sqrt{a x + b} }\right)^{m - 2} }$$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b squared by p x + q
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)} = \frac 1 {b p - a q} \left({\frac 1 {a x + b} + \frac p {b p - a q} \ln \left\vert{\frac {p x + q} {a x + b} }\right\vert}\right) + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)}$$
$$= \int \left({\frac 1 {b p - a q} \left({\frac {-a p} {\left({b p - a q}\right) \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {-a} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {p^2} {\left({b p - a q}\right) \left({p x + q}\right)} }\right)}\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {b p - a q} \left({\frac {-a p} {b p - a q} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} - a \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {p^2} {b p - a q} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p x + q} }\right)$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {b p - a q} \left({\frac {-a p} {b p - a q} \frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - a \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {p^2} {b p - a q} \frac 1 p \ln \left\vert{p x + q}\right\vert }\right) + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $a x + b$
$$= \frac 1 {b p - a q} \left({\frac {-p} {b p - a q} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert - a \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac p {b p - a q} \ln \left\vert{p x + q}\right\vert }\right) + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $\left({a x + b}\right)^2$
$$= \frac 1 {b p - a q} \left({\frac 1 {a x + b} + \frac p {b p - a q} \ln \left\vert{\frac {p x + q} {a x + b} }\right\vert}\right) + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of x squared over a x + b squared by p x + q
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)} = \frac {b^2} {\left({b p - a q}\right) a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {\left({b p - a q}\right)^2} \left({\frac {q^2} p \ln \left\vert{p x + q}\right\vert + \frac {b \left({b p - 2 a q}\right)} {a^2} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert}\right) + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)}$$
$$= \int \left({\frac {-b^2} {a \left({b p - a q}\right) \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {q^2} {\left({b p - a q}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)} + \frac {b \left({b p - 2 a q}\right)} {a \left({b p - a q}\right)^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac {-b^2} {a \left({b p - a q}\right)} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} + \frac {q^2} {\left({b p - a q}\right)^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p x + q} + \frac {b \left({b p - 2 a q}\right)} {a \left({b p - a q}\right)^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
We have:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)}$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $\left({a x + b}\right)^2$
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p x + q} = \frac 1 p \ln \left \vert {p x + q} \right \vert$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $a x + b$
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x + b} = \frac 1 a \ln \left \vert {a x + b} \right \vert$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $a x + b$
Therefore:
$$\int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)}$$
$$= \frac {-b^2} {a \left({b p - a q}\right)} \frac {-1} {a \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {q^2} {\left({b p - a q}\right)^2} \left({\frac 1 p \ln \left\vert{p x + q}\right\vert}\right) + \frac {b \left({b p - 2 a q}\right)} {a \left({b p - a q}\right)^2} \left({\frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert}\right) + C$$
Substitution
$$= \frac {b^2} {\left({b p - a q}\right) a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {\left({b p - a q}\right)^2} \left({\frac {q^2} p \ln \left\vert{p x + q}\right\vert + \frac {b \left({b p - 2 a q}\right)} {a^2} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert}\right) + C$$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Power of a x + b by Power of p x + q
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^n} = \frac {-1} {\left({n - 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\frac 1 {\left({a x + b}\right)^{m-1} \left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} } + a \left({m + n - 2}\right) \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} } }\right)$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $a x + b$ by Power of $p x + q$: Increment of Power:
$\displaystyle \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac 1 {\left({n + 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\left({a x + b}\right)^{m+1} \left({p x + q}\right)^{n+1} - a \left({m + n + 2}\right) \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{n+1} \ \mathrm d x}\right)$
Setting $m := -m$ and $n := -n$:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^n}$$
$$= \int \left({a x + b}\right)^{-m} \left({p x + q}\right)^{-n} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= \frac 1 {\left({-n + 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\left({a x + b}\right)^{-m+1} \left({p x + q}\right)^{-n+1} - a \left({-m - n + 2}\right) \int \left({a x + b}\right)^{-m} \left({p x + q}\right)^{-n+1} \ \mathrm d x}\right)$$
$$= \frac {-1} {\left({n - 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\frac 1 {\left({a x + b}\right)^{m-1} \left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} } + a \left({m + n - 2}\right) \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} } }\right)$$

title: Primitive of Power of a x + b over Power of p x + q/Formulation 1
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^m} {\left({p x + q}\right)^n} \rd x = \frac {-1} {\left({n - 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{m + 1} } {\left({p x + q}\right)^{n - 1} } + \left({n - m - 2}\right) a \int \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^m} { \left({p x + q}\right)^{n - 1} } \rd x}\right)$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $a x + b$ by Power of $p x + q$: Increment of Power:
$\displaystyle \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^n \rd x = \frac 1 {\left({n + 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\left({a x + b}\right)^{m + 1} \left({p x + q}\right)^{n + 1} - \left({m + n + 2}\right) a \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{n + 1} \rd x}\right)$
Setting $n := -n$:
$$\int \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^m} {\left({p x + q}\right)^n} \rd x$$
$$= \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{-n} \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {\left({-n + 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\left({a x + b}\right)^{m + 1} \left({p x + q}\right)^{-n + 1} - \left({m + -n + 2}\right) a \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{-n + 1} \rd x}\right)$$
$$= \frac {-1} {\left({n - 1}\right) \left({b p - a q}\right)} \left({\frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{m + 1} } {\left({p x + q}\right)^{n - 1} } + \left({n - m - 2}\right) a \int \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^m} {\left({p x + q}\right)^{n - 1} } }\right)$$

title: Primitive of Power of a x + b over Power of p x + q/Formulation 2
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^m} {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x = \frac {-1} {\paren {n - m - 1} p} \paren {\frac {\paren {a x + b}^m} {\paren {p x + q}^{n - 1} } + m \paren {b p - a q} \int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{m - 1} } {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x}$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $a x + b$ by Power of $p x + q$: Decrement of Power:
$\displaystyle \int \paren {a x + b}^m \paren {p x + q}^n \rd x = \frac {\paren {a x + b}^m \paren {p x + q}^{n + 1} } {\paren {m + n + 1} a} + \frac {m \paren {b p - a q} } {\paren {m + n + 1} p} \int \paren {a x + b}^{m - 1} \paren {p x + q}^n \rd x$
Setting $n := -n$:
$$\int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^m} {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x$$
$$= \int \paren {a x + b}^m \paren {p x + q}^{-n} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {\paren {a x + b}^m \paren {p x + q}^{-n + 1} } {\paren {m - n + 1} p} + \frac {m \paren {b p - a q} } {\paren {m - n + 1} p} \int \paren {a x + b}^{m - 1} \paren {p x + q}^{-n} \rd x$$
$$= \frac {-1} {\paren {n - m - 1} p} \paren {\frac {\paren {a x + b}^m} {\paren {p x + q}^{n - 1} } + m  \paren {b p - a q} \int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{m - 1} } {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x}$$

title: Primitive of Root of a x + b over p x + q
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\sqrt{a x + b} } {p x + q} \rd x = \begin{cases}
\dfrac {2 \sqrt{a x + b} } p + \dfrac {\sqrt {b p - a q} } {p \sqrt p} \ln \size {\dfrac {\sqrt {p \paren {a x + b} } - \sqrt {b p - a q} } {\sqrt {p \paren {a x + b} } + \sqrt {b p - a q} } } & : b p - a q > 0 \\
\dfrac {2 \sqrt{a x + b} } p - \dfrac {\sqrt {a q - b p} } {p \sqrt p} \arctan \sqrt {\dfrac {p \paren {a x + b} } {a q - b p} } & : b p - a q < 0 \\
\end{cases}$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Power of $a x + b$ over Power of $p x + q$: Formulation 2:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^m} {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x = \frac {-1} {\paren {n - m - 1} p} \paren {\frac {\paren {a x + b}^m} {\paren {p x + q}^{n - 1} } + m \paren {b p - a q} \int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{m - 1} } {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x}$
Setting $m := \dfrac 1 2$ and $n = 1$:
$$\int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {\paren {p x + q}^n} \rd x = \frac {-1} {\paren {1 - \frac 1 2 - 1} p} \paren {\frac {\paren {a x + b}^{1/2} } {\paren {p x + q}^0} + \frac 1 2 \paren {b p - a q} \int \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{1/2 - 1} } {\paren {p x + q} } \rd x}$$
$$= \frac {2 \sqrt {a x + b} } p + \frac {b p - a q} p \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {a x + b} \paren {p x + q} }$$
From Primitive of Reciprocal of $p x + q$ by Root of $a x + b$:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {p x + q} \sqrt{a x + b} } = \begin{cases}
\dfrac 1 {\sqrt {b p - a q} \sqrt p} \ln \size {\dfrac {\sqrt {p \paren {a x + b} } - \sqrt {b p - a q} } {\sqrt {p \paren {a x + b} } + \sqrt {b p - a q} } } & : b p - a q > 0 \\
\dfrac 2 {\sqrt {a q - b p} \sqrt p} \arctan \sqrt {\dfrac {p \paren {a x + b} } {a q - b p} } & : b p - a q < 0 \\
\end{cases}$
The result follows by substitution.

title: Primitive of Power of p x + q by Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \paren {p x + q}^n \sqrt {a x + b} \rd x = \frac {2 \paren {p x + q}^{n + 1} \sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {2 n + 3} p} + \frac {b p - a q} {\paren {2 n + 3} p} \int \frac {\paren {p x + q}^n} {\sqrt{a x + b} } \rd x$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $a x + b$ by Power of $p x + q$: Decrement of Power:
$\displaystyle \int \paren {a x + b}^m \paren {p x + q}^n \rd x = \frac {\paren {a x + b}^m \paren {p x + q}^{n + 1} } {\paren {m + n + 1} p} + \frac {m \paren {b p - a q} } {\paren {m + n + 1} p} \int \paren {a x + b}^{m - 1} \paren {p x + q}^n \rd x$
Setting $m := \dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \paren {a x + b}^{1 / 2} \paren {p x + q}^n \rd x = \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{1 / 2} \paren {p x + q}^{n + 1} } {\paren {\frac 1 2 + n + 1} p} + \frac {\dfrac 1 2 \paren {b p - a q} } {\paren {\frac 1 2 + n + 1} p} \int \paren {a x + b}^{1 / 2 - 1} \paren {p x + q}^n \rd x$$
$$= \frac {2 \paren {p x + q}^{n + 1} \sqrt {a x + b} } {\paren {2 n + 3} p} + \frac {b p - a q} {\paren {2 n + 3} p} \int \frac {\paren {p x + q}^n} {\sqrt {a x + b} } \rd x$$

title: Primitive of Power of p x + q over Root of a x + b
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\left({p x + q}\right)^n} {\sqrt{a x + b} } \ \mathrm d x = \frac {2 \left({p x + q}\right)^n \sqrt{a x + b} } {\left({2 n + 1}\right) a} + \frac {2 n \left({a q - b p}\right)} {\left({2 n + 1}\right) a} \int \frac {\left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} } {\sqrt{a x + b} } \ \mathrm d x$
proof_text:
From Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of $a x + b$ by Power of $p x + q$: Decrement of Power:
$\displaystyle \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{m+1} \left({p x + q}\right)^n} {\left({m + n + 1}\right) a} - \frac {n \left({b p - a q}\right)} {\left({m + n + 1}\right) a} \int \left({a x + b}\right)^m \left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} \ \mathrm d x$
Setting $m := -\dfrac 1 2$:
$$\int \frac {\left({p x + q}\right)^n} {\sqrt{a x + b} } \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{-1/2 + 1} \left({p x + q}\right)^n} {\left({-\frac 1 2 + n + 1}\right) a} - \frac {n \left({b p - a q}\right)} {\left({-\frac 1 2 + n + 1}\right) a} \int \left({a x + b}\right)^{-1/2} \left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= \frac {2 \left({p x + q}\right)^n \sqrt{a x + b} } {\left({2 n + 1}\right) a} + \frac {2 n \left({a q - b p}\right)} {\left({2 n + 1}\right) a} \int \frac {\left({p x + q}\right)^{n-1} } {\sqrt{a x + b} } \ \mathrm d x$$

title: Primitive of x over x squared plus a squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} = \frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} + C$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Power of x less one over Power of x plus Power of a:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \rd x} {x^n + a^n} = \frac 1 n \ln \size {x^n + a^n} + C$
So:
$$\int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} = \frac 1 2 \ln \size {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^{n - 1} } {\paren {x^n + a^n} }$ with $n = 2$
$$= \frac 1 2 \, \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Absolute Value of Even Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x squared plus a squared
theorem_text: $\ds \int \frac {\rd x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^2 x} - \frac x {a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} x - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \size x - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \size x - \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac 1 2 \, \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x squared plus a squared
theorem_text: $\ds \int \frac {\rd x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = \int \frac {a^2 \rd x} {a^2 x \paren {x^2 + a^2} }$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^2$
$$= \int \frac {\paren {x^2 + a^2 - x^2} \rd x} {a^2 x \paren {x^2 + a^2} }$$
adding and subtracting $x^2$
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\paren {x^2 + a^2} \rd x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} }$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} x - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \size x - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \size x - \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x squared plus a squared
theorem_text: $\ds \int \frac {\rd x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of x plus Power of a:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)} = \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^n} {x^n + a^n} }\right\vert + C$
So:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^2 + a^2}\right)} = \frac 1 {2 a^2} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)}$ with $n = 2$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2} \ln \left({\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right) + C$$
Absolute Value of Even Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x squared plus a squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = -\frac 1 {a^2 x} - \frac 1 {a^3} \arctan \frac x a + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {1 \rd x} {x^2 + a^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= -\frac 1 {a^2 x} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= -\frac 1 {a^2 x} - \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac 1 a \arctan \frac x a} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $x^2 + a^2$
$$= -\frac 1 {a^2 x} - \frac 1 {a^3} \arctan \frac x a + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x squared plus a squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^2 + a^2}\right)} = -\frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 + a^2} {x^2} }\right) + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^2 + a^2}\right)} = \int \left({\frac 1 {a^2 x^3} - \frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac x {a^4 \left({x^2 + a^2}\right)} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 + a^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {-1} {a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 + a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-1} {a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac 1 2 \ln \left ({x^2 + a^2}\right)}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= -\frac 1 {a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({x^2}\right) + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left ({x^2 + a^2}\right) + C$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= -\frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 + a^2} {x^2} }\right) + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x squared plus a squared squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} = \frac 1 {2 a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^4 x} - \frac x {a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac x {a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} x - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln x - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln x - \frac 1 {a^4} \paren {\frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln x - \frac 1 {a^4} \paren {\frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {-\frac 1 {2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {\left({x^2 + a^2}\right)^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$$
simplification

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x squared plus a squared squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} = -\frac 1 {a^4 x} - \frac x {2 a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 3 {2 a^5} \arctan \frac x a + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 + a^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \frac {-1} x - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 + a^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= -\frac 1 {a^4 x} - \frac 1 {a^4} \paren {\frac 1 a \arctan \frac x a} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $x^2 + a^2$
$$= -\frac 1 {a^4 x} - \frac 1 {a^5} \arctan \frac x a - \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac x {2 a^2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a^3} \arctan \frac x a} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2$
$$= -\frac 1 {a^4 x} - \frac x {2 a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 3 {2 a^5} \arctan \frac x a + C$$
simplification

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x squared plus a squared squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} = -\frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} = \int \paren {-\frac 2 {a^6 x} + \frac 1 {a^4 x^3} + \frac {2 x} {a^6 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } + \frac x {a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= -\frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {\d x} x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^3} + \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= -\frac 2 {a^6} \ln x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^3} + \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= -\frac 2 {a^6} \ln x - \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 + a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= -\frac 2 {a^6} \ln x - \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 2 {a^6} \paren {\frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= -\frac 2 {a^6} \ln x - \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {x^2 + a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \paren {-\frac 1 {2 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {\paren {x^2 + a^2}^2}$
$$= -\frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4 \paren {x^2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 + a^2} } + C$$
simplification

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x squared minus a squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 - a^2} } = \frac 1 {2 a^2} \, \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2} } + C$
for $x^2 > a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 - a^2} } = \int \paren {\frac x {a^2 \paren {x^2 - a^2} }  - \frac 1 {a^2 x} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {\d x} x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} - \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \size x + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} } - \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \size x + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 - a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^2} \ln \size {x^2} + C$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {x^2} + C$$
as $x^2 > 0$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x squared minus a squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} = \frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2} }\right) + C$
for $x^2 > a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} = \int \left({\frac {-1} {a^2 x^3} - \frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac x {a^4 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac {-1} {a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 - a^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 - a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 - a^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac 1 2 \ln \left ({x^2 -a^2}\right)}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 - a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({x^2}\right) + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left ({x^2 - a^2}\right) + C$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 x^2} + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2} }\right) + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared minus a squared squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x^2 - a^2}\right)^2} = \frac {-x} {2 a^2 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + C$
for $x^2 > a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {\left({x^2 - a^2}\right)^2} = \int \left({\frac 1 {4 a^3 \left({x + a}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a^3 \left({x - a}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a^2 \left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^2 \left({x - a}\right)^2} }\right) \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \int \frac {\d x} {x + a} - \frac 1 {4 a^3} \int \frac {\d x} {x - a} + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left\vert{x + a}\right\vert - \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left\vert{x - a}\right\vert + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Function of $a x + b$ and Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right\vert + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2} + C$$
Difference of Logarithms
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2} + C$$
Sign of Quotient of Factors of Difference of Squares
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \frac {-1} {\left({x + a}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a^2} \frac {-1} {\left({x - a}\right)} + C$$
Primitive of Function of $a x + b$ and Primitive of Power
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) - \left({\frac 1 {4 a^2 \left({x + a}\right)} + \frac 1  {4 a^2 \left({x - a}\right)} }\right) + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) - \left({\frac {\left({x - a}\right) + \left({x + a}\right)} {4 a^2 \left({x + a}\right) \left({x - a}\right)} }\right) + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-x} {2 a^2 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + C$$
Difference of Two Squares

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x squared minus a squared squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} = \frac {-1} {2 a^2 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^2} {x^2 - a^2} }\right) + C$
for $x^2 > a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} = \int \left({\frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac {-x} {a^4 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } + \frac x {a^2 \paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} }\right) \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} x + \frac {-1} {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \size x + \frac {-1} {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \size x + \frac {-1} {a^4} \paren {\frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 - a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \size x  + \frac {-1} {2 a^4} \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac {-1} {2 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {x^2} + \frac {-1} {2 a^4} \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac {-1} {2 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } } + C$$
Logarithm of Power and $x^2 > 0$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^2 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 - a^2} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x squared minus a squared squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {a^4 x} - \frac x {2 a^4 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + C$
for $x^2 > a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)^2} = \int \left({\frac 1 {a^4 x^2} + \frac 3 {4 a^5 \left({x + a}\right)} - \frac 3 {4 a^5 \left({x - a}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a^4 \left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4 \left({x - a}\right)^2} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x + a} - \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x - a} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \frac {-1} x + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x + a} - \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x - a} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{x + a}\right\vert - \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{x - a}\right\vert + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x - a}\right)^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{x + a}\right\vert - \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{x - a}\right\vert + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \frac {-1} {x + a} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \frac {-1} {x - a} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right\vert + \frac {-1} {4 a^4 \left({ x + a}\right)} + \frac {-1} {4 a^4 \left({x - a}\right)} + C$$
Difference of Logarithms
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + \frac {-1} {4 a^4 \left({ x + a}\right)} + \frac {-1} {4 a^4 \left({x - a}\right)} + C$$
Sign of Quotient of Factors of Difference of Squares
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} - \frac x {2 a^4 \left({x^2 - a^2}\right)} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \left({\frac {x + a} {x - a} }\right) + C$$
simplification

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x squared minus a squared squared
theorem_text:
$\ds \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} = \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 - a^2} } + C$
for $x^2 > a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^4 x^3} + \frac 2 {a^6 x} - \frac {2 x} {a^6 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } + \frac x {a^4 \paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^3} + \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {\d x} x - \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \frac {-1} {2 x^2} + \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {\d x} x - \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 2 {a^6} \ln \size x - \frac 2 {a^6} \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 2 {a^6} \ln \size x - \frac 2 {a^6} \frac 1 2 \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^2 - a^2}$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 2 {a^6} \ln \size x - \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \frac {-1} {2 \paren {x^2 - a^2} }  + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {\paren {x^2 - a^2}^2}$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {x^2} - \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {x^2 - a^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \frac {-1} {2 \paren {x^2 - a^2} }  + C$$
Logarithm of Power and $x^2 > 0$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4 \paren {x^2 - a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^6} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {x^2 - a^2} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Sign of Quotient of Factors of Difference of Squares
theorem_text:
Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a \ne b$.
Then
$\map \sgn {a^2 - b^2} = \map \sgn {\dfrac {a + b} {a - b} } = \map \sgn {\dfrac {a - b} {a + b} }$
where $\sgn$ denotes the signum of a real number.
proof_text:
$$\map \sgn {\frac {a - b} {a + b} } = \map \sgn {a - b} \frac 1 {\map \sgn {a + b} }$$
Signum Function is Completely Multiplicative
$$= \map \sgn {a - b} \map \sgn {a + b}$$
Signum Function of Reciprocal
$$= \map \sgn {\paren {a - b} \paren {a + b} }$$
Signum Function is Completely Multiplicative
$$= \map \sgn {a^2 - b^2}$$
Difference of Two Squares
$$= \map \sgn {\paren {a + b} \paren {a - b} }$$
Difference of Two Squares
$$= \map \sgn {a + b} \map \sgn {a - b}$$
Signum Function is Completely Multiplicative
$$= \map \sgn {a + b} \frac 1 {\map \sgn {a - b} }$$
Signum Function of Reciprocal
$$= \map \sgn {\frac {a + b} {a - b} }$$
Signum Function is Completely Multiplicative

title: Absolute Value Function is Completely Multiplicative
theorem_text:
The absolute value function on the real numbers $\R$ is completely multiplicative:
$\forall x, y \in \R: \left\vert{x y}\right\vert = \left\vert{x}\right\vert \, \left\vert{y}\right\vert$
where $\left \vert{a}\right \vert$ denotes the absolute value of $a$.
proof_text:
We have the result Multiplicative Group of Reals is Subgroup of Complex.
Therefore, any result applying to all complex numbers will also hold for all real numbers.
The result follows from Complex Modulus of Product of Complex Numbers.

title: Primitive of x cubed over a squared minus x squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {a^2 - x^2} = -\frac {x^2} 2 - \frac {a^2} 2 \ln \left({a^2 - x^2}\right) + C$
for $x^2 < a^2$.
proof_text:
Let:
$$\int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {a^2 - x^2} = \int \frac {x \left({x^2 - a^2 + a^2}\right)} {a^2 - x^2} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= \int \frac {-x \left({a^2 - x^2}\right)} {a^2 - x^2} \ \mathrm d x + \int \frac {a^2 x} {a^2 - x^2} \ \mathrm d x$$
$$= -\int x \ \mathrm d x + a^2 \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {a^2 - x^2}$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= -\frac {x^2} 2 + a^2 \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {a^2 - x^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= -\frac {x^2} 2 + a^2 \left({-\frac 1 2 \ln \left({a^2 - x^2}\right)}\right) + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal of $\dfrac x {a^2 - x^2}$
$$= -\frac {x^2} 2 - \frac {a^2} 2 \ln \left({a^2 - x^2}\right) + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a squared minus x squared squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} = \frac 1 {2 a^2 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {a^2 - x^2} } + C$
for $x^2 < a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac x {a^4 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } + \frac x {a^2 \paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {a^2 - x^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {a^2 - x^2}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \size x + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \rd x} {a^2 - x^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \size x + \frac 1 {a^4} \paren {-\frac 1 2 \map \ln {a^2 - x^2} } + \frac 1 {a^2} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {a^2 - x^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \ln \size x - \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {a^2 - x^2} + \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac 1 {2 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {\paren {a^2 - x^2}^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {a^2 - x^2} + \frac 1 {2 a^2 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } + C$$
Logarithm of Power and $x^2 > 0$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^2 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a^4} \map \ln {\frac {x^2} {a^2 - x^2} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by a squared minus x squared squared
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} = \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac x {2 a^4 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \map \ln {\frac {a + x} {a - x} } + C$
for $x^2 < a^2$.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {a^2 - x^2}^2} = \int \paren {\frac 1 {a^4 x^2} + \frac 3 {4 a^5 \paren {a + x} } + \frac 3 {4 a^5 \paren {a - x} } + \frac 1 {4 a^4 \paren {a + x}^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4 \paren {a - x}^2} } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\d x} {a + x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\d x} {a - x} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + x}^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a - x}^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \frac {-1} x + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\d x} {a + x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \int \frac {\d x} {a - x} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + x}^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a - x}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \size {a + x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \paren {-\ln \size {a - x} } + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + x}^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a - x}^2} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \size {a + x} - \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \size {a - x} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \frac {-1} {a + x} + \frac 1 {4 a^4} \frac 1 {a - x} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \ln \size {\frac {a + x} {a - x} } + \frac {-1} {4 a^4 \paren {a + x} } + \frac 1 {4 a^4 \paren {a - x} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \map \ln {\frac {a + x} {a - x} } + \frac {-1} {4 a^4 \paren {a + x} } + \frac 1 {4 a^4 \paren {a - x} } + C$$
Sign of Quotient of Factors of Difference of Squares
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} + \frac x {2 a^4 \paren {a^2 - x^2} } + \frac 3 {4 a^5} \map \ln {\frac {a + x} {a - x} } + C$$
simplification

title: Primitive of x over a x squared plus b x plus c
theorem_text:
Let $a \in \R_{\ne 0}$.
Then:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{a x^2 + b x + c}\right\vert - \frac b {2 a} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}$
proof_text:
First note that by Derivative of Power:
$(1): \quad \dfrac {\mathrm d} {\mathrm d x} \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right) = 2 a x + b$
Then:
