$$\int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 1 {2a} \int \frac {2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \frac 1 {2a} \int \frac {\left({2 a x + b - b}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}$$
$$= \frac 1 {2a} \int \frac {\left({2 a x + b}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} - \frac b {2a} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {2a}\ln \left\vert{a x^2 + b x + c}\right\vert - \frac b {2a} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}$$
Primitive of Function under its Derivative and $(1)$

title: Ring of Sets Closed under Finite Union
theorem_text:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a ring of sets.
Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n \in \mathcal R$.
Then:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j \in \mathcal R$
proof_text:
Proof by induction:
For all $n \in \N_{>0}$, let $P \left({n}\right)$ be the proposition:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j \in \mathcal R$
$P(1)$ is true, as this just says $A_1 \in \mathcal R$.
Basis for the Induction
$P(2)$ is the case:
$A_1 \cup A_2 \in \mathcal R$
which is immediate, from definition 2 of ring of sets.
This is our basis for the induction.
Induction Hypothesis
Now we need to show that, if $P \left({k}\right)$ is true, where $k \ge 2$, then it logically follows that $P \left({k+1}\right)$ is true.
So this is our induction hypothesis:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^k A_j \in \mathcal R$
Then we need to show:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^{k+1} A_j \in \mathcal R$
Induction Step
This is our induction step:
We have that:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^{k+1} A_j = \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^k A_j \cup A_{k+1}$
But from the induction hypothesis we have that:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^k A_j \in \mathcal R$
Hence from the basis for the induction, it follows that:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^{k+1} A_j \in \mathcal R$
So $P \left({k}\right) \implies P \left({k+1}\right)$ and the result follows by the Principle of Mathematical Induction.
Therefore:
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j \in \mathcal R$

title: Gamma Function for Non-Negative Integer Argument
theorem_text:
The Gamma function satisfies:
$\map \Gamma z = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {z + 1} } z$
for any $z$ which is not a nonpositive integer.
proof_text:
From Gamma Difference Equation:
$\map \Gamma {z + 1} = z \, \map \Gamma z$
which is valid for all $z \notin \Z_{\le 0}$.
The result follows by dividing by $z$.

title: Sum of Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence
theorem_text:
Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be an arithmetic-geometric sequence defined as:
$a_k = \paren {a + k d} r^k$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$
Then its closed-form expression is:
$\displaystyle \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + \frac {r d \paren {1 - n r^{n - 1} + \paren {n - 1} r^n} } {\paren {1 - r}^2}$
proof_text:
$$\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} r^k = a \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} r^k + d \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} k r^k$$
$$= \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + d \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} k r^k$$
Sum of Geometric Sequence
$$= \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + d \paren {\frac {\paren {n - 1} r^{n + 1} - n r^n + r} {\paren {r - 1}^2} }$$
Sum of Sequence of Power by Index
Hence the result, after algebra.

title: Sum of Infinite Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence
theorem_text:
Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be an arithmetic-geometric sequence defined as:
$a_k = \paren {a + k d} r^k$ for $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$
Let:
$\size r < 1$
where $\size r$ denotes the absolute value of $r$.
Then:
$\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac a {1 - r} + \frac {r d} {\paren {1 - r}^2}$
proof_text:
From Sum of Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence, we have:
$\displaystyle s_n = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + \frac {r d \paren {1 - n r^{n - 1} + \paren {n - 1} r^n} } {\paren {1 - r}^2}$
We have that $\size r < 1$.
So by Sequence of Powers of Number less than One:
$r^n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$
and
$r^{n - 1} \to 0$ as $n - 1 \to \infty$
Hence:
$s_n \to \dfrac a {1 - r} + \dfrac {r d} {\paren {1 - r}^2}$
as $n \to \infty$.
The result follows.

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Root of a x squared plus b x plus c
theorem_text:
Let $a \in \R_{\ne 0}$.
Then:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = \begin{cases}
\dfrac {-1} {\sqrt c} \ln \left({\dfrac {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} x}\right) & : b^2 - 4 a c > 0 \\
\dfrac {-1} {\sqrt c} \sinh^{-1} \left({\dfrac {b x + 2 c} {\left\vert{x}\right\vert \sqrt {4 a c - b^2} } }\right) & : b^2 - 4 a c < 0 \\
\dfrac {-1} {\sqrt c} \ln \left\vert{\dfrac {2 c} x + b}\right\vert + C & : b^2 - 4 a c = 0
\end{cases}$
proof_text:
$$x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac x {\paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} }$$
$$= \frac{x \paren {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} } {\paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} \paren {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} }$$
$$= \frac{x \paren {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} } {2 \sqrt c + \paren {b x + 2 c} \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} }$$
$$= \frac N D$$
where:
$$N = \frac {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} x$$
$$D = \frac {2 \sqrt c + \paren {b x + 2 c} \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} } {x^2}$$
Then:
$$\frac {\d N} {\d x} = \frac {x \paren {\sqrt c \paren {2 a x + b} \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} + b} - \paren {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} } {x^2}$$
$$= \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} \frac {\paren {\sqrt c \paren {2 a x^2 + b x} + b x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } - \paren {2 \sqrt c \paren {a x^2 + b x + c} + \paren {b x + 2 c} \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } } {x^2}$$
$$= \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} \frac {\paren {\sqrt c \paren {2 a x^2 + b x - 2 a x^2 - 2 b x - 2 c} + b x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } - \paren {\paren {b x + 2 c} \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } } {x^2}$$
$$= \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} \frac {\paren {\sqrt c \paren {-b x - 2 c} - \paren {\paren {2 c} \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } } } {x^2}$$
$$= -\frac {2 c + \sqrt c \paren {b x + 2 c} \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^{-\frac 1 2} } {x^2}$$
$$= \sqrt c \times D$$
Now provided $N$ is real and non zero:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = \int \frac D N \rd x$$
$$= \frac {-1} {\sqrt c} \int \frac {\frac {\d N} {\d x} } N \rd x$$
$$= \frac {-1} {\sqrt c} \ln \size N$$
Primitive of Function under its Derivative
$$= \frac {-1} {\sqrt c} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {2 \sqrt c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + b x + 2 c} } x}$$

title: Primitive of x over x cubed plus a cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 {6 a} \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a x + a^2} {\paren {x + a}^2} } + \frac 1 {a \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {x \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \int \frac {\paren {x + a - a} \rd x} {x^3 + a^3}$$
$$= \int \frac {\paren {x + a} \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} - a \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \int \frac {\paren {x + a} \rd x} {\paren {x + a} \paren {x^2 - a x + a^2} } - a \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3}$$
Sum of Two Cubes
$$= \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a x + a^2} - a \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 2 {a \sqrt 3} \arctan \paren {\frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3} } - a \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x^2 - a x + a^2}$
$$= \frac 2 {a \sqrt 3} \, \map \arctan {\frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3} } - a \paren {\frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^2 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3} }$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x^3 + a^3}$
$$= \frac 2 {a \sqrt 3} \, \map \arctan {\frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3} } - \frac 1 {6 a} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } - \frac 1 {a \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {6 a} \, \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a x + a^2} {\paren {x + a}^2} } + \frac 1 {a \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}$$
gathering terms

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed plus a cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^2 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3} = \int \paren {\frac 1 {3 a^2 \paren {x + a} } - \frac {x - 2 a} {3 a^2 \paren {x^2 - a x + a^2} } } \rd x$$
Partial Fraction Expansion
$$= \int \paren {\frac 1 {3 a^2 \paren {x + a} } - \frac {2 x - 4 a} {6 a^2 \paren {x^2 - a x + a^2} } } \rd x$$
multiplying top and bottom by $2$
$$= \int \paren {\frac 1 {3 a^2 \paren {x + a} } - \paren {\frac {2 x - a} {6 a^2 \paren {x^2 - a x + a^2} } } - \paren {\frac {3 a} {6 a^2 \paren {x^2 - a x + a^2} } } } \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {3 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {x + a} - \frac 1 {6 a^2} \int \frac {\paren {2 x - a} \rd x} {x^2 - a x + a^2} + \frac 1 {2 a} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a x + a^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {3 a^2} \ln \size {x + a} - \frac 1 {6 a^2} \int \frac {\paren {2 x - a} \rd x} {x^2 - a x + a^2} + \frac 1 {2 a} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a x + a^2}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {a x + b}$
$$= \frac 1 {3 a^2} \ln \size {x + a} - \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {x^2 - a x + a^2} + \frac 1 {2 a} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a x + a^2}$$
Primitive of Function under its Derivative
$$= \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\paren {x + a}^2} - \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {x^2 - a x + a^2} + \frac 1 {2 a} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a x + a^2}$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a x + a^2}$$
Difference of Logarithms
$$= \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \paren {\frac 2 {a \sqrt 3} \map \arctan {\frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3} } }$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x^2 - a x + a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^2 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of x squared over x cubed plus a cubed
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 3 \ln \size {x^3 + a^3} + C$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Power of x less one over Power of x plus Power of a:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \rd x} {x^n + a^n} = \frac 1 n \ln \size {x^n + a^n} + C$
So:
$$\int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 3 \ln \size {x^3 + a^3} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^{n - 1} } {\paren {x^n + a^n} }$ with $n = 3$
directly.

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x cubed plus a cubed squared
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \frac 1 {3 a^3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} + \frac 1 {3 a^6} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^3} {x^3 + a^3} }\right\vert$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \int \frac {a^3 \ \mathrm d x} {a^3 x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^3$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^3 + a^3 - x^3}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^3 x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2}$$
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} - \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} - \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \left({\frac 1 {3 a^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^3} {x^3 + a^3} }\right\vert}\right) - \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)}$
$$= \frac 1 {a^3} \left({\frac 1 {3 a^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^3} {x^3 + a^3} }\right\vert}\right) - \frac 1 {a^3} \left({\frac {-1} {3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} }\right)$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^2} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {3 a^3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} + \frac 1 {3 a^6} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^3} {x^3 + a^3} }\right\vert$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of x cubed over x fourth plus a fourth
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Power of x less one over Power of x plus Power of a:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \ \mathrm d x} {x^n + a^n} = \frac 1 n \ln \left\vert{x^n + a^n}\right\vert + C$
So:
$$\int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac 1 4 \ln \left\vert{x^4 + a^4}\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^{n - 1} } {\left({x^n + a^n}\right)}$ with $n = 4$
$$= \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4 + C$$
Absolute Value of Even Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x fourth plus a fourth
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {4 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^4} {x^4 + a^4} }\right)$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of x plus Power of a:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)} = \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^n} {x^n + a^n} }\right\vert + C$
So:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^2 + a^2}\right)} = \frac 1 {4 a^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^4} {x^4 + a^4} }\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)}$ with $n = 4$
$$= \frac 1 {4 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^4} {x^4 + a^4} }\right) + C$$
Absolute Value of Even Power
directly.

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x fourth plus a fourth
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \frac {-1} {a^4 x} - \frac {-1} {4 a^5 \sqrt 2} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} {x^2 + a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} }\right) + \frac 1 {2 a^5 \sqrt 2} \left({\arctan \left({1 - \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right) - \arctan \left({1 + \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right)}\right)$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \int \frac {a^4 \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^4$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^4 + a^4 - x^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\left({x^4 + a^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^4 \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac {-1} x}\right) - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4}$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} - \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac 1 {4 a \sqrt 2} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} {x^2 + a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} }\right) - \frac 1 {2 a \sqrt 2} \left({\arctan \left({1 - \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right) - \arctan \left({1 + \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right)}\right) }\right)$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^2} {x^4 + a^4}$
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4 x} - \frac {-1} {4 a^5 \sqrt 2} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} {x^2 + a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} }\right) + \frac 1 {2 a^5 \sqrt 2} \left({\arctan \left({1 - \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right) - \arctan \left({1 + \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right)}\right)$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x fourth plus a fourth
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^6} \arctan \frac {x^2} {a^2}$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \int \frac {a^4 \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^4$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^4 + a^4 - x^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\left({x^4 + a^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^4 \ \mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3} - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac {-1} {2 x} }\right) - \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4}$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac 1 {2 a^2} \arctan \frac {x^2} {a^2} }\right)$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^4 + a^4}$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^6} \arctan \frac {x^2} {a^2}$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x fourth minus a fourth
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac 1 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x - a} {x + a} }\right\vert + \frac 1 {2 a^5} \arctan \frac x a + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \int \frac {a^4 \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^4$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^4 + a^4 - x^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^4 - \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4} \int \frac {\left({x^4 - a^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^4 \ \mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 - a^4}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4} \left({\frac {-1} x}\right) + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 - a^4}$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x - a} {x + a} }\right\vert + \frac 1 {2 a} \arctan \frac x a }\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^2} {x^4 - a^4}$
$$= \frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac 1 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x - a} {x + a} }\right\vert + \frac 1 {2 a^5} \arctan \frac x a + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x fourth minus a fourth
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^6} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \int \frac {a^4 \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^4$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^4 + a^4 - x^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^4 - \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^4 x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4} \int \frac {\left({x^4 - a^4}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x^4 \ \mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3} + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 - a^4}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-1} {a^4} \left({\frac {-1} {2 x} }\right) + \frac 1 {a^4} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 - a^4}$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 1 {a^4} \left({\frac 1 {4 a^2} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right\vert}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac x {x^4 - a^4}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^6} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right\vert + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of x plus Power of a
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)} = \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^n} {x^n + a^n} }\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)} = \int \frac {a^n \ \mathrm d x} {a^n x \left({x^2 + a^2}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^n$
$$= \int \frac {\left({x^n + a^n - x^n}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {a^n x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)}$$
adding and subtracting $x^n$
$$= \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {\left({x^n + a^n}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)} - \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {x^n \ \mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x - \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \ \mathrm d x} {x^n + a^n}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {a^n} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \ \mathrm d x} {x^n + a^n} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac 1 {a^n} \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert - \frac 1 {a^n} \left({\frac 1 n \ln \left\vert{x^n + a^n}\right\vert }\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^{n - 1}} {x^n + a^n}$
$$= \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left\vert{x^n}\right\vert - \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left\vert{x^n + a^n}\right\vert + C$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left({\frac {x^n} {x^n + a^n} }\right) + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Absolute Value of Even Power
theorem_text:
Let $x \in \R$ be a real number.
Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer.
Then:
$\left\vert{x^{2 n} }\right\vert = x^{2 n}$
proof_text:
From Even Power is Non-Negative:
$x^{2 n} \ge 0$
The result follows from the definition of absolute value.

title: Primitive of x cubed over x fourth plus a fourth/Proof 2
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4$
proof_text:
From Primitive of Power of x less one over Power of x plus Power of a:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \ \mathrm d x} {x^n + a^n} = \frac 1 n \ln \left\vert{x^n + a^n}\right\vert + C$
So:
$$\int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac 1 4 \ln \left\vert{x^4 + a^4}\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^{n - 1} } {\left({x^n + a^n}\right)}$ with $n = 4$
$$= \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4 + C$$
Absolute Value of Even Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of x minus Power of a
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^n - a^n} } = \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \size {\frac {x^n - a^n} {x^n} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^n - a^n} } = \int \frac {a^n \rd x} {a^n x \paren {x^2 - a^2} }$$
multiplying top and bottom by $a^n$
$$= \int \frac {\paren {-\paren {x^n - a^n} + x^n} \rd x} {a^n x \paren {x^n - a^n} }$$
adding and subtracting $x^n$
$$= \frac {-1} {a^n} \int \frac {\paren {x^n - a^n} \rd x} {x \paren {x^n - a^n} } + \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {x^n \rd x} {x \paren {x^n - a^n} }$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {-1} {a^n} \int \frac {\d x} x + \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \rd x} {x^n - a^n}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-1} {a^n} \ln \size x + \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \rd x} {x^n - a^n} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-1} {a^n} \ln \size x + \frac 1 {a^n} \paren {\frac 1 n \ln \size {x^n - a^n} } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {x^{n - 1}} {x^n - a^n}$
$$= \frac {-1} {n a^n} \ln \size {x^n} + \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \size {x^n - a^n} + C$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \size {\frac {x^n - a^n} {x^n} } + C$$
Difference of Logarithms

title: Primitive of Cube of Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \sin^3 a x \rd x = -\frac {\cos a x} a + \frac {\cos^3 a x} {3 a} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \sin^3 a x \rd x = \int \paren {\frac {3 \sin a x - \sin 3 a x} 4} \rd x$$
Power Reduction Formula for Cube of Sine
$$= \frac 3 4 \int \sin a x \rd x - \frac 1 4 \int \sin 3 a x \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 3 4 \paren {\frac {-\cos a x} a} - \frac 1 4 \paren {\frac {-\cos 3 a x} {3 a} } + C$$
Primitive of $\sin a x$
$$= \frac {-3 \cos a x} {4 a} + \frac 1 {12 a} \paren {\cos 3 a x} + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-3 \cos a x} {4 a} + \frac 1 {12 a} \paren {4 \cos^3 a x - 3 \cos a x} + C$$
Triple Angle Formula for Cosine
$$= \frac {-3 \cos a x} {4 a} + \frac {\cos^3 a x} {3 a} - \frac {\cos a x} {4 a} + C$$
multipying out
$$= -\frac {\cos a x} a + \frac {\cos^3 a x} {3 a} + C$$
simplifying

title: Derivative of Periodic Function
theorem_text:
Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function.
Let $f$ be differentiable on all of $\R$.
Then if $f$ is periodic with period $L$, then its derivative is also periodic with period $L$.
proof_text:
Let $f$ be differentiable on all of $\R$.
Let $f$ be periodic with period $L$.
Then taking the derivative of both sides using the Chain Rule for Derivatives yields:
$\map f x = \map f {x + L} \implies \map {f'} x = \map {f'} {x + L}$
Let $L'$ be the period of $f'$.
Suppose that $\size {L'} < \size L$.
$f$ is differentiable and therefore continuous, by Differentiable Function is Continuous.
From Image of Closed Real Interval is Bounded, it follows that $f$ is bounded on $\closedint 0 {\size L}$.
But from the General Periodicity Property, it follows that $f$ is bounded on all of $\R$.
Then from Primitive of Periodic Function, it follows that $L'$ is the period of $f$.
But we had previously established that $L$ was the period of $f$.
This is a contradiction, therefore $L' = L$.
Hence the result.

title: One Plus Tangent Half Angle over One Minus Tangent Half Angle
theorem_text: $\dfrac {1 + \tan \frac x 2} {1 - \tan \frac x 2} = \sec x + \tan x$
proof_text:
$$\frac {1 + \tan \frac x 2}{1 - \tan \frac x 2} = \frac {1 + \frac {\sin \frac x 2}{\cos \frac x 2} }{1 - \frac {\sin \frac x 2}{\cos \frac x 2} }$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \frac {\cos \frac x 2 + \sin \frac x 2}{\cos \frac x 2 - \sin \frac x 2}$$
multiply top and bottom by $\cos \dfrac x 2$
$$= \frac {\cos \frac x 2 + \sin \frac x 2}{\cos \frac x 2 - \sin \frac x 2} \times \frac {\cos \frac x 2 + \sin \frac x 2}{\cos \frac x 2 + \sin \frac x 2}$$
$$= \frac{\cos^2 \frac x 2 + \sin^2 \frac x 2 + 2 \cos \frac x 2 \sin \frac x 2}{\cos^2 \frac x 2 - \sin^2 \frac x 2}$$
$$= \frac{1 + 2 \cos \frac x 2 \sin \frac x 2}{\cos^2 \frac x 2 - \sin^2 \frac x 2}$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}$$
Double Angle Formula for Sine, Double Angle Formula for Cosine
$$= \sec x + \tan x$$
Sum of Secant and Tangent

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared plus square of q by Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 + q^2 \sin^2 a x} = \frac 1 {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \arctan \frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \tan a x} p + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p^2 + q^2 \sin^2 a x} = \int \frac {\sec^2 a x \rd x} {p^2 \sec^2 a x + q^2 \tan^2 a x}$$
multiplying numerator and denominator by $\sec^2 a x$
$$= \int \frac {\sec^2 a x \rd x} {p^2 + \paren {p^2 + q^2} \tan^2 a x}$$
Difference of Squares of Secant and Tangent
$$= \int \frac {\paren {\tan a x}' \rd x} {a p^2 + a \paren {p^2 + q^2} \tan^2 a x}$$
Derivative of Tangent Function
$$= \int \frac {\d t} {a p^2 + a \paren {p^2 + q^2} t^2}$$
substituting $t = \tan a x$
$$= \frac 1 {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \int \frac {\rd t} {\paren {\tfrac p {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } }^2 + t^2}$$
$$= \frac 1 {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p t} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= \frac 1 {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p t} + C$$
$$= \frac 1 {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \tan a x} p} + C$$
substituting $t = \tan a x$

title: Primitive of Cosine of a x over x
theorem_text:
$$\int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} x = \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\paren {-1}^k \paren {a x}^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k} \paren {2 k}!} + C$$
$$= \ln \size x - \frac {\paren {a x}^2} {2 \times 2!} + \frac {\paren {a x}^4} {4 \times 4!} - \frac {\paren {a x}^6} {6 \times 6!} - \cdots + C$$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} x = \int \frac 1 x \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \paren {-1}^k \frac {\paren {a x}^{2 k} }{\paren {2 k}!} } \rd x$$
Definition of Real Cosine Function
$$= \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^k a^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k}!} \int \frac 1 x \paren {x^{2 k} } \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
(1) $$= \int \frac {\rd x} x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^k a^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k}!} \int \paren {x^{2 k - 1} } \rd x$$
extracting case for $k = 0$
$$= \int \frac {\d x} x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^k a^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k}!} \frac {x^{2 k} } {2 k} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \int \frac {\d x} x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\paren {-1}^k \paren {a x}^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k} \paren {2 k}!} + C$$
simplifying
$$= \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\paren {-1}^k \paren {a x}^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k} \paren {2 k}!} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
The validity of $(1)$ follows from Cosine Function is Absolutely Convergent.

title: Primitive of Cube of Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \cos^3 a x \rd x = \frac {\sin a x} a - \frac {\sin^3 a x} {3 a} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \cos^3 a x \rd x = \int \left({\frac {3 \cos a x + \cos 3 a x} 4}\right) \rd x$$
Power Reduction Formula for $\cos^3$
$$= \frac 3 4 \int \cos a x \rd x + \frac 1 4 \int \cos 3 a x \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 3 4 \left({\frac {\sin a x} a}\right) + \frac 1 4 \left({\frac {\sin 3 a x} {3 a} }\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\cos a x$
$$= \frac {3 \sin a x} {4 a} + \frac 1 {12 a} \left({\sin 3 a x}\right) + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {3 \sin a x} {4 a} + \frac 1 {12 a} \left({3 \sin a x - 4 \sin^3 a x}\right) + C$$
Triple Angle Formula for Sine
$$= \frac {3 \sin a x} {4 a} + \frac {\sin a x} {4 a} - \frac {\sin^3 a x} {3 a} + C$$
multipying out
$$= \frac {\sin a x} a - \frac {\sin^3 a x} {3 a} + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of 1 minus Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 - \cos a x}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {2a} \cot \frac {a x} 2 - \frac 1 {6 a} \cot^3 \frac {a x} 2 + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 - \cos a x}\right)^2} = \int \left({\frac 1 2 \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2}\right)^2 \ \mathrm d x$$
Reciprocal of One Minus Cosine
$$= \frac 1 4 \int \csc^4 \frac {a x} 2 \ \mathrm d x$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 4 \left({\frac{-\csc^2 \dfrac {a x} 2 \cot \dfrac {a x} 2} {\dfrac {3 a} 2} + \frac 2 3 \int \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2 \ \mathrm d x}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\csc^n a x$
$$= \frac {-1} {6 a} \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2 \cot \dfrac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 6 \int \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2 \ \mathrm d x + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-1} {6 a} \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2 \cot \dfrac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 6 \left({\frac {-2} a \cot \frac {a x} 2}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\csc^2 a x$
$$= \frac {-1} {6 a} \left({1 + \cot^2 \frac {a x} 2}\right) \cot \dfrac {a x} 2 - \frac 2 {6 a} \cot \frac {a x} 2 + C$$
Difference of Squares of Cosecant and Cotangent
$$= \frac {-1} {2a} \cot \frac {a x} 2 - \frac 1 {6 a} \cot^3 \frac {a x} 2 + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of 1 plus Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 + \cos a x}\right)^2} = \frac 1 {2a} \tan \frac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 {6 a} \tan^3 \frac {a x} 2 + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 + \cos a x}\right)^2} = \int \left({\frac 1 2 \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2}\right)^2 \ \mathrm d x$$
Reciprocal of One Plus Cosine
$$= \frac 1 4 \int \sec^4 \frac {a x} 2 \ \mathrm d x$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 4 \left({\frac{\sec^2 \dfrac {a x} 2 \tan \dfrac {a x} 2} {\dfrac {3 a} 2} + \frac 2 3 \int \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2 \ \mathrm d x}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\sec^n a x$
$$= \frac 1 {6 a} \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2 \tan \dfrac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 6 \int \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2 \ \mathrm d x + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {6 a} \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2 \tan \dfrac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 6 \left({\frac 2 a \tan \frac {a x} 2}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\sec^2 a x$
$$= \frac 1 {6 a} \left({1 + \tan^2 \frac {a x} 2}\right) \tan \dfrac {a x} 2 + \frac 2 {6 a} \tan \frac {a x} 2 + C$$
Difference of Squares of Secant and Tangent
$$= \frac 1 {2a} \tan \frac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 {6 a} \tan^3 \frac {a x} 2 + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared plus square of q by Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 + q^2 \cos^2 a x} = \frac 1 {a p \sqrt{p^2 + q^2} } \arctan \frac {p \tan a x} {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p^2 + q^2 \cos^2 a x} = \int \frac {\csc^2 a x \rd x} {p^2 \csc^2 a x + q^2 \cot^2 a x}$$
multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $\sec^2 a x$.
$$= \int \frac {\csc^2 a x \rd x} {p^2 + \paren {p^2 + q^2} \cot^2 a x}$$
Difference of Squares of Cosecant and Cotangent
$$= \int \frac {-\paren {\cot a x}' \rd x} {a p^2 + a \paren {p^2 + q^2} \cot^2 a x}$$
Derivative of Cotangent Function
$$= \int \frac {-\d t} {a p^2 + a \paren {p^2 + q^2} t^2}$$
putting $t = \cot a x$
$$= \frac {-1} {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \int \frac {\d t} {\paren {\tfrac p {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } }^2 + t^2}$$
$$= \frac {-1} {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p \, \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p t } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {x^2 + a^2}$
$$= \frac {-1} {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p t} + C$$
$$= \frac {-1} {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } p \cot a x} + C$$
substituting $t = \cot a x$
$$= \frac {-1} {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } {p \tan a x} } + C$$
$$= \frac {-1} {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arccot {\frac {p \tan a x} {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } } + C$$
Arctangent of Reciprocal equals Arccotangent
$$= \frac 1 {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \paren {\map \arctan {\frac {p \tan a x} {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } } - \frac \pi 2} + C$$
Sum of Arctangent and Arccotangent
$$= \frac 1 {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {p \tan a x} {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } } + C$$
absorbing into the arbitrary constant

title: Primitive of Sine of a x by Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \sin a x \cos a x \rd x = \frac {\sin^2 a x} {2 a} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \sin a x \cos a x \rd x = \int \frac {\sin 2 a x} 2 \rd x$$
Double Angle Formula for Sine
$$= \frac {-\cos 2 a x} {4 a} + C$$
Primitive of $\cos a x$
$$= \frac {-\paren {1 - 2 \sin^2 a x} } {4 a} + C$$
Double Angle Formula for Cosine: Corollary 2
$$= \frac {-1} {4 a} + \frac {\sin^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
separating fraction
$$= \frac {\sin^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
subsuming $\dfrac {-1} {4 a}$ into arbitrary constant

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Sine of a x by Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin a x \cos a x} = \frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{\tan a x}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin a x \cos a x} = \int \frac {\sec a x \ \mathrm d x} {\sin a x}$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\sec^2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {\sin a x \sec a x}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\sec a x$
$$= \int \frac {\sec^2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {\frac {\sin a x} {\cos a x} }$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\sec^2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {\tan a x}$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{\tan a x}\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {\sec^2 a x} {\tan a x}$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of Sine of a x by Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {\sin^2 a x \cos a x} = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } - \frac 1 {a \sin a x} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {\sin^2 a x \cos a x} = \int \frac {\paren {\sin^2 a x + \cos^2 a x} \rd x} {\sin^2 a x \cos a x}$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\sin^2 a x \rd x} {\sin^2 a x \cos a x} + \int \frac {\cos^2 a x \rd x} {\sin^2 a x \cos a x}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \int \frac {\d x} {\cos a x} + \int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} {\sin^2 a x}$$
simplifying
$$= \int \sec a x \rd x + \int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} {\sin^2 a x}$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \int \sec a x \rd x + \int \frac {\cot a x \rd x} {\sin a x}$$
Cotangent is Cosine divided by Sine
$$= \int \sec a x \rd x + \int \csc a x \cot a x \rd x$$
Cosecant is Reciprocal of Sine
$$= \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + \int \csc a x \cot a x \rd x + C$$
Primitive of $\sec a x$
$$= \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } - \frac 1 {a \sin a x} + C$$
Primitive of $\csc^n a x \cot a x$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of Sine of a x by Square of Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {\sin^2 a x \cos^2 a x} = \frac {-2 \cot 2 a x} a + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {\sin^2 a x \cos^2 a x} = \int \frac {\d x} {\left({\sin a x \cos a x}\right)^2}$$
$$= \int \frac {\d x} {\left({\frac {\sin 2 a x} 2}\right)^2}$$
Double Angle Formula for Sine
$$= 4 \int \frac {\d x} {\sin^2 2 a x}$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= 4 \int \csc^2 2 a x \rd x$$
Cosecant is Reciprocal of Sine
$$= 4 \frac {-\cot 2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
Primitive of Square of Cosecant of a x
$$= \frac {-2 \cot 2 a x} a + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Square of Sine of a x over Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\sin^2 a x \rd x} {\cos a x} = \frac {-\sin a x} a + \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\sin^2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {\cos a x} = \int \frac {\paren {1 - \cos^2 a x} \rd x} {\cos a x}$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos a x} - \int \cos a x \ \mathrm d x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \int \sec a x \ \mathrm d x - \int \cos a x \ \mathrm d x$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \frac {-\sin a x} a + \int \sec a x \ \mathrm d x + C$$
Primitive of $\cos a x$
$$= \frac {-\sin a x} a + \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C$$
Primitive of $\sec a x$

title: Primitive of Square of Cosine of a x over Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\cos^2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {\sin a x} = \frac {\cos a x} a + \frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{\tan \frac {a x} 2}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\cos^2 a x \ \mathrm d x} {\sin a x} = \int \frac {\left({1 - \sin^2 a x}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {\sin a x}$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin a x} - \int \sin a x \ \mathrm d x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \int \csc a x \ \mathrm d x - \int \sin a x \ \mathrm d x$$
Cosecant is Reciprocal of Sine
$$= \frac {\cos a x} a + \int \csc a x \ \mathrm d x + C$$
Primitive of $\sin a x$
$$= \frac {\cos a x} a + \frac 1 a \ln \left\vert{\tan \frac {a x} 2}\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\csc a x$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Cosine of a x by 1 plus Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos a x \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} = \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan \left({\frac {a x} 2 + \frac \pi 4}\right)}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$u = \sin a x$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = a \cos a x$$
Derivative of $\sin a x$
Then:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos a x \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} = \int \frac {\cos a x \ \mathrm d x} {\cos^2 a x \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\cos a x$
$$= \int \frac {\cos a x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({1 - \sin^2 a x}\right) \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)}$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {\left({1 - u^2}\right) \left({1 + u}\right)}$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {\left({1 - u}\right) \left({1 + u}\right)^2}$$
Difference of Two Squares
$$= \frac 1 a \left({\frac 1 {-2} \left({\frac 1 {1 + u} + \frac {-1} {-2} \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 - u} {1 + u} }\right\vert}\right)}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)}$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + u}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 - u} {1 + u} }\right\vert + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 - \sin a x} {1 + \sin a x} }\right\vert + C$$
substituting for $u$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {\frac 1 2 \sec^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2}\right)} {\frac 1 2 \sec^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} }\right\vert + C$$
Reciprocal of $1 - \sin$ and Reciprocal of $1 + \sin$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac{\cos^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} {\cos^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2}\right)} }\right\vert + C$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac{\cos^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} {\sin^2 \left({\frac \pi 2 - \left({\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2}\right)}\right)} }\right\vert + C$$
Sine of Complement equals Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac{\cos^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} {\sin^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} }\right\vert + C$$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {\sin^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} {\cos^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right)} }\right\vert + C$$
Logarithm of Reciprocal
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan^2 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right) }\right\vert + C$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 + \sin a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right) }\right\vert + C$$
Logarithm of Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Cosine of a x by 1 minus Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {\cos a x \paren {1 - \sin a x} } = \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac {a x} 2 + \frac \pi 4} } + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$u = \sin a x$$
$$\frac {\d u} {\d x} = a \cos a x$$
Derivative of $\sin a x$
Then:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {\cos a x \paren {1 - \sin a x} } = \int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} {\cos^2 a x \paren {1 - \sin a x} }$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\cos a x$
$$= \int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} {\paren {1 - \sin^2 a x} \paren {1 - \sin a x} }$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\d u} {\paren {1 - u^2} \paren {1 - u} }$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\d u} {\paren {1 + u} \paren {1 - u}^2}$$
Difference of Two Squares
$$= \frac 1 a \paren {\frac 1 2 \paren {\frac 1 {1 - u} + \frac 1 2 \ln \size {\frac {1 + u} {1 - u} } } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\paren {a x + b}^2 \paren {p x + q} }$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - u} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {1 + u} {1 - u} } + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {1 + \sin a x} {1 - \sin a x} } + C$$
substituting for $u$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {\frac 1 2 \map {\sec^2} {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } {\frac 1 2 \map {\sec^2} {\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2} } } + C$$
Reciprocal of $1 - \sin$ and Reciprocal of $1 + \sin$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {\map {\cos^2} {\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2} } {\map {\cos^2} {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } } + C$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {\map {\sin^2} {\frac \pi 2 - \paren {\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2} } } {\map {\cos^2} {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } } + C$$
Sine of Complement equals Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {\map {\sin^2} {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } {\map {\cos^2} {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } } + C$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\map {\tan^2} {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 - \sin a x} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C$$
Logarithm of Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Sine of a x by 1 plus Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {\sin a x \paren {1 + \cos a x} } = \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + \cos a x} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \size {\tan \frac {a x} 2} + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$u = \cos a x$$
$$\frac {\d u} {\d x} = -a \sin a x$$
Derivative of $\cos a x$
Then:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {\sin a x \paren {1 + \cos a x} } = \int \frac {\sin a x \rd x} {\sin^2 a x \paren {1 + \cos a x} }$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\sin a x$
$$= \int \frac {\sin a x \rd x} {\paren {1 - \cos^2 a x} \paren {1 + \cos a x} }$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} a \int \frac {\d u} {\paren {1 - u^2} \paren {1 + u} }$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac {-1} a \int \frac {\d u} {\paren {1 - u} \paren {1 + u}^2}$$
Difference of Two Squares
$$= \frac {-1} a \paren {\frac 1 {-2} \paren {\frac 1 {1 + u} + \frac {-1} {-2} \ln \size {\frac {1 - u} {1 + u} } } } + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\paren {a x + b}^2 \paren {p x + q} }$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + u} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {1 - u} {1 + u} } + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + \cos a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {1 - \cos a x} {1 + \cos a x} } + C$$
substituting for $u$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + \cos a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {\frac 1 2 \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2} {\frac 1 2 \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2} } + C$$
Reciprocal of $1 - \cos$ and Reciprocal of $1 + \cos$
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + \cos a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {\sin^2 \frac {a x} 2} {\cos^2 \frac {a x} 2} } + C$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + \cos a x} } + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\tan^2 \frac {a x} 2} + C$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {2 a \paren {1 + \cos a x} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \size {\tan \frac {a x} 2} + C$$
Logarithm of Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of Sine of a x by 1 minus Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin a x \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} = \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan \frac {a x} 2}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
Let:
$$u = \cos a x$$
$$\frac {\mathrm d u} {\mathrm d x} = -a \sin a x$$
Derivative of $\cos a x$
Then:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin a x \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} = \int \frac {\sin a x \ \mathrm d x} {\sin^2 a x \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\sin a x$
$$= \int \frac {\sin a x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({1 - \cos^2 a x}\right) \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)}$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} a \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {\left({1 - u^2}\right) \left({1 - u}\right)}$$
Integration by Substitution
$$= \frac {-1} a \int \frac {\mathrm d u} {\left({1 + u}\right) \left({1 - u}\right)^2}$$
Difference of Two Squares
$$= \frac {-1} a \left({\frac 1 2 \left({\frac 1 {1 - u} + \frac 1 2 \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 + u} {1 - u} }\right\vert}\right)}\right) + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {\left({a x + b}\right)^2 \left({p x + q}\right)}$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - u}\right)} - \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 + u} {1 - u} }\right\vert + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - u}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 - u} {1 + u} }\right\vert + C$$
Logarithm of Power
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {1 - \cos a x} {1 + \cos a x} }\right\vert + C$$
substituting for $u$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {\frac 1 2 \sec^2 \frac {a x} 2} {\frac 1 2 \csc^2 \frac {a x} 2} }\right\vert + C$$
Reciprocal of $1 - \cos$ and Reciprocal of $1 + \cos$
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\frac {\sin^2 \frac {a x} 2} {\cos^2 \frac {a x} 2} }\right\vert + C$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan^2 \frac {a x} 2}\right\vert + C$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \frac {-1} {2 a \left({1 - \cos a x}\right)} + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan \frac {a x} 2}\right\vert + C$$
Logarithm of Power

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p by Sine of a x plus q by Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} = \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \tan \left\vert{\frac {a x + \arctan \dfrac q p} 2}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} = \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \cos \left({a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q}\right)}$$
Multiple of Sine plus Multiple of Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \int \sec \left({a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q}\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
$$= \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \int \sec z \ \mathrm d z$$
Primitive of Function of $a x + b$: $z = a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q$
$$= \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \tan \left\vert{\frac z 2 + \frac \pi 4}\right\vert + C$$
Primitive of $\sec a x$
$$= \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \tan \left\vert{\frac 1 2 \left({a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q + \frac \pi 2}\right)}\right\vert + C$$
substituting for $z$
$$= \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \tan \left\vert{\frac {a x + \arctan \dfrac q p} 2}\right\vert + C$$
Lemma

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p by Sine of a x plus q by Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} = \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \tan \left\vert{\frac {a x + \arctan \dfrac q p} 2}\right\vert + C$
proof_text:
Let $z = a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q$.
Then:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x + r} = \int \frac {\d x} {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \map \cos {a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q} }$$
Multiple of Sine plus Multiple of Cosine
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\d z} {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \cos z}$$
Primitive of Function of $a x + b$
Let $d = \sqrt {p^2 + q^2}$.
Then:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x + r}$$
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\d z} {r + d \cos z}$$
$$= \frac 1 a \begin{cases} 
\ds \frac 2 {\sqrt {r^2 - d^2} } \map \arctan {\sqrt {\frac {r + d} {r - d} } \tan \dfrac z 2} + C & : r^2 > d^2 \\
\ds \frac 1 {\sqrt {d^2 - r^2} } \ln \size {\frac {\tan \dfrac z 2 + \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } {\tan \dfrac z 2 - \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } } + C & : r^2 < d^2 \\
\end{cases}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {p + q \cos a x}$
$$= \begin{cases} 
\ds \frac 2 {a \sqrt {r^2 - p^2 - q^2} } \map \arctan {\sqrt {\frac {r + d} {r - d} } \tan \dfrac z 2} + C & : r^2 > p^2 + q^2 \\
\ds \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2 - r^2} } \ln \size {\frac {\tan \dfrac z 2 + \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } {\tan \dfrac z 2 - \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } } + C & : r^2 < p^2 + q^2 \\
\end{cases}$$
partly substituting for $d$
Then:
$$\sqrt {\frac {r + d} {r - d} } \tan \frac z 2 = \sqrt {\frac {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } {r - \sqrt {p^2 - q^2} } } \tan \frac z 2$$
substituting for $d$
$$= \sqrt {\frac {\paren {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} }^2} {\paren {r - \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \paren {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } } } \tan \frac z 2$$
multiplying top and bottom by $r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2}$
$$= \frac {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } {\sqrt {r^2 - p^2 - q^2} } \tan \frac z 2$$
Difference of Two Squares
Then:
$$\tan \frac z 2 = \map \tan {\frac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 2 \arctan \frac {-p} q}$$
substituting for $z$
$$= \frac {\tan \dfrac {a x} 2 + \map \tan {\frac 1 2 \arctan \frac {-p} q} } {1 - \tan \dfrac {a x} 2 \map \tan {\frac 1 2 \arctan \frac {-p} q} }$$
Tangent of Sum

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p by Sine of a x plus q by Cosine of a x plus r
theorem_text:
$\ds \int \frac {\d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x + r} = \begin{cases}
\ds \frac 2 {a \sqrt {r^2 - p^2 - q^2} } \map \arctan {\frac {p + \paren {r - q} \tan \dfrac {a x} 2} {\sqrt {r^2 - p^2 - q^2} } } + C & : p^2 + q^2 < r^2 \\
\ds \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2 - r^2} } \ln \size {\frac {p - \sqrt {p^2 + q^2 - r^2} + \paren {r - q} \tan \dfrac {a x} 2} {p + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2 - r^2} + \paren {r - q} \tan \dfrac {a x} 2} } + C & : p^2 + q^2 > r^2
\end{cases}$
proof_text:
Let $z = a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q$.
Then:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x + r} = \int \frac {\d x} {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \map \cos {a x + \arctan \dfrac {-p} q} }$$
Multiple of Sine plus Multiple of Cosine
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\d z} {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \cos z}$$
Primitive of Function of $a x + b$
Let $d = \sqrt {p^2 + q^2}$.
Then:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x + r}$$
$$= \frac 1 a \int \frac {\d z} {r + d \cos z}$$
$$= \frac 1 a \begin{cases} 
\ds \frac 2 {\sqrt {r^2 - d^2} } \map \arctan {\sqrt {\frac {r + d} {r - d} } \tan \dfrac z 2} + C & : r^2 > d^2 \\
\ds \frac 1 {\sqrt {d^2 - r^2} } \ln \size {\frac {\tan \dfrac z 2 + \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } {\tan \dfrac z 2 - \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } } + C & : r^2 < d^2 \\
\end{cases}$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {p + q \cos a x}$
$$= \begin{cases} 
\ds \frac 2 {a \sqrt {r^2 - p^2 - q^2} } \map \arctan {\sqrt {\frac {r + d} {r - d} } \tan \dfrac z 2} + C & : r^2 > p^2 + q^2 \\
\ds \frac 1 {a \sqrt {p^2 + q^2 - r^2} } \ln \size {\frac {\tan \dfrac z 2 + \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } {\tan \dfrac z 2 - \sqrt {\dfrac {d - r} {d + r} } } } + C & : r^2 < p^2 + q^2 \\
\end{cases}$$
partly substituting for $d$
Then:
$$\sqrt {\frac {r + d} {r - d} } \tan \frac z 2 = \sqrt {\frac {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } {r - \sqrt {p^2 - q^2} } } \tan \frac z 2$$
substituting for $d$
$$= \sqrt {\frac {\paren {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} }^2} {\paren {r - \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \paren {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } } } \tan \frac z 2$$
multiplying top and bottom by $r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2}$
$$= \frac {r + \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } {\sqrt {r^2 - p^2 - q^2} } \tan \frac z 2$$
Difference of Two Squares
Then:
$$\tan \frac z 2 = \map \tan {\frac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 2 \arctan \frac {-p} q}$$
substituting for $z$
$$= \frac {\tan \dfrac {a x} 2 + \map \tan {\frac 1 2 \arctan \frac {-p} q} } {1 - \tan \dfrac {a x} 2 \map \tan {\frac 1 2 \arctan \frac {-p} q} }$$
Tangent of Sum

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared by square of Sine of a x plus q squared by square of Cosine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 \sin^2 a x + q^2 \cos^2 a x} = \frac 1 {a p q} \map \arctan {\frac {p \tan a x} q} + C$
proof_text:
Let $u = p^2 + q^2$ and $v = q^2 - p^2$.
Then:
(1) $$u + v = 2 q^2$$
(2) $$u - v = 2 p ^2$$
Also:
$$u^2 - v^2 = \paren {u + v} \paren {u - v}$$
$$u^2 - v^2 = \paren {2 q^2} \paren {2 p^2}$$
from $\paren 1$ and $\paren 2$
(3) $$u^2 - v^2 = 4 p^2 q^2$$
Therefore:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p^2 \sin^2 a x + q^2 \cos^2 a x} = \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 \paren {\frac {1 - \cos 2 a x} 2} + q^2 \cos^2 a x}$$
Square of Sine
$$= \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 \paren {\frac {1 - \cos 2 a x} 2} + q^2 \paren {\frac {1 + \cos 2 a x} 2} }$$
Square of Cosine
$$= \int \frac {2 \d x} {p^2 - p^2 \cos 2 a x + q^2 + q^2 \cos 2 a x}$$
$$= \int \frac {2 \d x} {p^2 + q^2 + \paren {q^2 - p^2} \cos 2 a x}$$
$$= 2 \paren { \frac 2 {\paren {2 a} \sqrt{u^2 - v^2} } } \map \arctan {\sqrt{ \frac {u - v} {u + v} } \tan \frac {\paren {2 a} x} 2} + C$$
Primitive of $\dfrac 1 {p + q \cos a x}$
$$= 2 \paren {\frac 1 {a \sqrt{4 p^2 q^2} } } \map \arctan {\sqrt{ \frac {2 p^2} {2 q^2} } \tan a x} + C$$
from $\paren 3$
$$= \paren {\frac 2 {2 a p q} } \map \arctan {\sqrt{ \frac {p^2} {q^2} } \tan a x} + C$$
$$= \paren {\frac 1 {a p q} } \map \arctan {\frac p q \tan a x} + C$$
$$= \frac 1 {a p q} \map \arctan {\frac {p \tan a x} q} + C$$

title: Primitive of Power of Sine of a x over Power of Cosine of a x/Reduction of Power of Cosine
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\sin^{m + 1} a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m - n + 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x + C$
proof_text:
$$\frac {\sin^{m + 1} a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x + C$$
$$= \int \frac {\sin^{m + 2} a x} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^n a x}$: Reduction of Both Powers
$$= \int \frac {\sin^m a x \left({1 - \cos^2 a x}\right)} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x - \int \frac {\sin^m a x \cos^2 a x} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x - \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x$$
simplifying
Hence, rearranging:
$$\int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^n a x} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\sin^{m + 1} a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x + \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x + C$$
$$= \frac {\sin^{m + 1} a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x - \frac {-n + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x + C$$
common denominator
$$= \frac {\sin^{m + 1} a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m - n + 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\sin^m a x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} \ \mathrm d x + C$$

title: Primitive of Power of Cosine of a x over Power of Sine of a x/Reduction of Power of Sine
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^n a x} \rd x = \frac {-\cos^{m + 1} a x} {a \paren {n - 1} \sin^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m - n + 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x + C$
proof_text:
$$\frac {-\cos^{m + 1} a x} {a \paren {n - 1} \sin^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x + C$$
$$= \int \frac {\cos^{m + 2} a x} {\sin^n a x} \rd x$$
Primitive of $\dfrac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^n a x}$: Reduction of Both Powers
$$= \int \frac {\cos^m a x \paren {1 - \sin^2 a x} } {\sin^n a x} \rd x$$
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^n a x} \rd x - \int \frac {\cos^m a x \sin^2 a x} {\sin^n a x} \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^n a x} \rd x - \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x$$
simplifying
Hence, rearranging:
$$\int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^n a x} \rd x = \frac {-\cos^{m + 1} a x} {a \paren {n - 1} \sin^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x + \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x + C$$
$$= \frac {-\cos^{m + 1} a x} {a \paren {n - 1} \sin^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x - \frac {-n + 1} {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x + C$$
common denominator
$$= \frac {-\cos^{m + 1} a x} {a \paren {n - 1} \sin^{n - 1} a x} - \frac {m - n + 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos^m a x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x} \rd x + C$$

title: Primitive of Cube of Tangent of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \tan^3 a x \rd x = \frac {\tan^2 a x} {2 a} + \frac 1 a \ln \size {\cos a x} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \tan^3 a x \rd x = \int \tan a x \tan^2 a x \rd x$$
$$= \int \tan a x \paren {\sec^2 a x - 1} \rd x$$
Difference of Squares of Secant and Tangent
$$= \int \tan a x \sec^2 a x \rd x - \int \tan a x \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {\tan^2 a x} {2 a} - \int \tan a x \rd x + C$$
Primitive of $\tan^n a x \sec^2 a x$: $n = 1$
$$= \frac {\tan^2 a x} {2 a} - \paren {\frac {-\ln \size {\cos a x} } a} + C$$
Primitive of $\tan a x$
$$= \frac {\tan^2 a x} {2 a} + \frac 1 a \ln \size {\cos a x} + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Tangent of a x over x
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\tan a x} x \ \mathrm d x = a x + \frac {\paren {a x}^3} 9 + \frac {2 \paren {a x}^5} {75} + \cdots + \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n - 1} \paren {2 n}!} + \cdots + C$
where $B_n$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli number.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\tan a x} x \ \mathrm d x = \int \frac 1 x \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \ \mathrm d x$$
Power Series Expansion for Tangent Function
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} B_{2 n} a^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \int  x^{2 n - 2} \ \mathrm d x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} B_{2 n} a^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \paren {\frac {x^{2 n - 1} } {2 n - 1} } + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n - 1} \paren {2 n}!} + C$$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p plus q by Tangent of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \tan a x} = \frac {p x} {p^2 + q^2} + \frac q {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \size {q \sin a x + p \cos a x} + C$
proof_text:
We have:
$\dfrac \d {\d x} \paren {q \sin a x + p \cos a x} = a q \cos a x - a p \sin a x$
Thus:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p + q \tan a x} = \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \dfrac {\sin a x} {\cos a x} }$$
Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
$$= \int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} {p \cos a x + q \sin a x}$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \int \frac {\paren {p^2 + q^2} \cos a x \rd x} {p \cos a x + q \sin a x}$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \int \frac {p^2 \cos a x + p q \sin a x - p q \sin a x + q^2 \cos a x} {p \cos a x + q \sin a x} \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \paren {\int \frac {p^2 \cos a x + p q \sin a x} {p \cos a x + q \sin a x} \ \d x + \int \frac {- p q \sin a x + q^2 \cos a x} {p \cos a x + q \sin a x} \rd x}$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \paren {\int p \rd x + \frac q a \int \frac {\map \d {p \cos a x + q \sin a x} } {p \cos a x + q \sin a x} }$$
$$= \frac {p x} {p^2 + q^2} + \frac q {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \size {p \cos a x + q \sin a x} + C$$
Primitive of Constant and Primitive of Reciprocal

title: Primitive of Cube of Cotangent of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \cot^3 a x \rd x = \frac {-\cot^2 a x} {2 a} - \frac 1 a \ln \size {\sin a x} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \cot^3 x \rd x = \int \cot a x \cot^2 a x \rd x$$
$$= \int \cot a x \paren {\csc^2 a x - 1} \rd x$$
Difference of Squares of Cosecant and Cotangent
$$= \int \cot a x \csc^2 a x \rd x - \int \cot a x \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac {-\cot^2 a x} {2 a} - \int \cot a x \rd x + C$$
Primitive of $\cot^n a x \csc^2 a x$: $n = 1$
$$= \frac {-\cot^2 a x} {2 a} - \paren {\frac {\ln \size {\sin a x} } a} + C$$
Primitive of $\cot a x$
$$= \frac {-\cot^2 a x} {2 a} - \frac 1 a \ln \size {\sin a x} + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Cotangent of a x over x
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\cot a x} x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {-1} a x - \frac {a x} 3 - \frac {\paren {a x}^3} {135} - \cdots - \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n - 1} \paren {2 n}!} - \cdots + C$
where $B_n$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli number.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\csc a x} x \ \mathrm d x = \int \frac 1 x \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n 2^{2 n} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \ \mathrm d x$$
Power Series Expansion for Cosecant Function
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n 2^{2 n} B_{2 n} a^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \int  x^{2 n - 2} \ \mathrm d x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n 2^{2 n} B_{2 n} a^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \paren {\frac {x^{2 n - 1} } {2 n - 1} } + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n 2^{2 n} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n - 1} \paren {2 n}!} + C$$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of p plus q by Cotangent of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \cot a x} = \frac {p x} {p^2 + q^2} - \frac q {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \size {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} + C$
proof_text:
We have:
$\dfrac \d {\d x} \paren {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} = a p \cos a x - a q \sin a x$
Thus:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {p + q \cot a x} = \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \dfrac {\cos a x} {\sin a x} }$$
Cotangent is Cosine divided by Sine
$$= \int \frac {\sin a x \rd x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x}$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \int \frac {\paren {p^2 + q^2} \sin a x \rd x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x}$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \int \frac {p^2 \sin a x + p q \cos a x - p q \cos a x + q^2 \sin a x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \paren {\int \frac {p^2 \sin a x + p q \cos a x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} \rd x + \int \frac {- p q \cos a x + q^2 \sin a x} {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} \rd x}$$
$$= \frac 1 {p^2 + q^2} \paren {\int p \rd x - \frac q a \int \frac {\map \d {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} } {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} }$$
$$= \frac {p x} {p^2 + q^2} - \frac q {a \paren {p^2 + q^2} } \ln \size {p \sin a x + q \cos a x} + C$$
Primitive of Constant and Primitive of Reciprocal

title: Primitive of Secant of a x over x
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\sec a x} x \ \mathrm d x = \ln \size x + \frac {\paren {a x}^2} 4 + \frac {5 \paren {a x}^4} {96} + \frac {61 \paren {a x}^6} {4320} + \cdots + \frac {\paren {-1}^n E_n \paren {a x}^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n} \paren {2 n}!} + \cdots + C$
where $E_n$ is the $n$th Euler number.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\csc a x} x \ \mathrm d x = \int \frac 1 x \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n E_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n}!} \ \rd x$$
Power Series Expansion for Cosecant Function
$$= \int \frac {E_0} x \ \rd x + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n E_{2 n} a^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n}!} \int  x^{2 n - 1} \ \rd x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \int \frac 1 x \ \rd x + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n E_{2 n} a^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n}!} \paren {\frac {x^{2 n} } {2 n} } + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \ln \size x + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^n E_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n} \paren {2 n}!} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of q plus p by Secant of a x
theorem_text: $\ds \int \frac {\d x} {q + p \sec a x} = \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \cos a x} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\d x} {q + p \sec a x} = \frac 1 q \int \frac {q \rd x} {q + p \sec a x}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $q$
$$= \frac 1 q \int \frac {\paren {q + p \sec a x - p \sec a x} \rd x} {q + p \sec a x}$$
$$= \frac 1 q \int \frac {\paren {q + p \sec a x} \rd x} {q + p \sec a x} - \frac p q \int \frac {\sec a x \rd x} {q + p \sec a x}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 q \int \d x - \frac p q \int \frac {\sec a x \rd x} {q + p \sec a x}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\sec a x \rd x} {q + p \sec a x} + C$$
Primitive of Constant
$$= \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\cos a x \sec a x \rd x} {q \cos a x + p \cos a x \sec a x} + C$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\cos a x$
$$= \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \cos a x} + C$$
Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine

title: Primitive of Cosecant of a x over x
theorem_text:
$\displaystyle \int \frac {\csc a x} x \rd x = \frac {-1} {a x} + \frac {a x} 6 + \frac {7 \paren {a x}^3} {1080} + \cdots + \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n - 1} \paren {2 n}!} + \cdots + C$
where $B_n$ is the $n$th Bernoulli number.
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\csc a x} x \ \mathrm d x = \int \frac 1 x \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \ \mathrm d x$$
Power Series Expansion for Cosecant Function
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} a^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \int  x^{2 n - 2} \ \mathrm d x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} a^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} \paren {\frac {x^{2 n - 1} } {2 n - 1} } + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n - 1} \paren {2 n}!} + C$$

title: Primitive of Reciprocal of q plus p by Cosecant of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x} = \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p + q \sin a x} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x} = \frac 1 q \int \frac {q \ \mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x}$$
multiplying top and bottom by $q$
$$= \frac 1 q \int \frac {\left({q + p \csc a x - p \csc a x}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x}$$
$$= \frac 1 q \int \frac {\left({q + p \csc a x}\right) \ \mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x} - \frac p q \int \frac {\csc a x \ \mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x}$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 q \int \mathrm d x - \frac p q \int \frac {\csc a x \ \mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x}$$
simplifying
$$= \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\csc a x \ \mathrm d x} {q + p \csc a x} + C$$
Primitive of Constant
$$= \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\sin a x \, \csc a x \ \mathrm d x} {q \sin a x + p \sin a x \, \csc a x} + C$$
multiplying top and bottom by $\sin a x$
$$= \frac x q - \frac p q \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p + q \sin a x} + C$$
Cosecant is Reciprocal of Sine

title: Primitive of Exponential of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int e^{a x} \rd x = \frac {e^{a x} } a + C$
proof_text:
$$\int e^{a x} \sin b x \rd x = \int e^{a x} \paren {\frac {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } {2 i} } \rd x$$
Sine Exponential Formulation
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{a x} \paren {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } \rd x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int \paren {e^{a x} e^{i b x} - e^{a x} e^{-i b x} } \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int \paren {e^{a x + i b x} - e^{a x - i b x} } \rd x$$
Exponent Combination Laws: Product of Powers
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{a x + i b x} \rd x - \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{a x - i b x} \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{\paren {a + i b} x} \rd x - \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{\paren {a - i b} x} \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{\paren {a + i b} x} } {a + i b} - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{\paren {a - i b} x} } {a - i b} + C$$
Primitive of $e^{a x}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x + i b x} } {a + i b} - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x - i b x} } {a - i b} + C$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} } {a + i b} - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{-i b x} } {a - i b} + C$$
Exponent Combination Laws: Product of Powers
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} \paren {a - i b} } {\paren {a + i b} \paren {a - i b} } - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{-i b x} \paren {a + i b} } {\paren {a - i b} \paren {a + i b} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} \paren {a - i b} - e^{a x} e^{-i b x} \paren {a + i b} } {2 i \paren {a + i b} \paren {a - i b} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} \paren {a - i b} - e^{a x} e^{-i b x} \paren {a + i b} } {2 i \paren {a^2 + b^2} } + C$$
Product of Complex Number with Conjugate
$$= \frac {a e^{a x} e^{i b x} - i b e^{a x} e^{i b x} - a e^{a x} e^{-i b x} - i b e^{a x} e^{-i b x} } {2 i \paren {a^2 + b^2} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {\frac {a e^{i b x} - i b e^{i b x} - a e^{-i b x} - i b e^{-i b x} } {2 i} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {a \frac {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } {2 i} - b \frac {e^{i b x} + e^{-i b x} } 2 } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {a \frac {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } {2 i} - b \cos b x } + C$$
Cosine Exponential Formulation
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {a \sin b x - b \cos b x } + C$$
Sine Exponential Formulation
$$= \frac {e^{a x} \paren {a \sin b x - b \cos b x} } {a^2 + b^2} + C$$

title: Primitive of Exponential of a x over x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \frac {e^{a x} \rd x} x = \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\paren {a x}^k} {k \times k!} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {e^{a x} \rd x} x = \int \frac 1 x \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {a x}^k} {k!} } \rd x$$
Power Series Expansion for Exponential Function
$$= \int \frac 1 x \paren {1 + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {a x}^k} {k!} } \rd x$$
extracting the case $k = 0$ from the expansion
(1) $$= \int \frac {\d x} x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a^k} {k!} \int x^{k - 1} \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a^k} {k!} \int x^{k - 1} \rd x$$
Primitive of Reciprocal
$$= \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a^k} {k!} \frac {x^k} k + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\paren {a x}^k} {k \times k!} + C$$
simplification
The validity of $(1)$ follows from absolute convergence of the power series expansion.

title: Primitive of Exponential of a x by Sine of b x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int e^{a x} \sin b x \rd x = \frac {e^{a x} \paren {a \sin b x - b \cos b x} } {a^2 + b^2} + C$
proof_text:
$$\int e^{a x} \sin b x \rd x = \int e^{a x} \paren {\frac {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } {2 i} } \rd x$$
Sine Exponential Formulation
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{a x} \paren {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } \rd x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int \paren {e^{a x} e^{i b x} - e^{a x} e^{-i b x} } \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int \paren {e^{a x + i b x} - e^{a x - i b x} } \rd x$$
Exponent Combination Laws: Product of Powers
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{a x + i b x} \rd x - \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{a x - i b x} \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{\paren {a + i b} x} \rd x - \frac 1 {2 i} \int e^{\paren {a - i b} x} \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{\paren {a + i b} x} } {a + i b} - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{\paren {a - i b} x} } {a - i b} + C$$
Primitive of $e^{a x}$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x + i b x} } {a + i b} - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x - i b x} } {a - i b} + C$$
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} } {a + i b} - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{-i b x} } {a - i b} + C$$
Exponent Combination Laws: Product of Powers
$$= \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} \paren {a - i b} } {\paren {a + i b} \paren {a - i b} } - \frac 1 {2 i} \frac {e^{a x} e^{-i b x} \paren {a + i b} } {\paren {a - i b} \paren {a + i b} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} \paren {a - i b} - e^{a x} e^{-i b x} \paren {a + i b} } {2 i \paren {a + i b} \paren {a - i b} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} e^{i b x} \paren {a - i b} - e^{a x} e^{-i b x} \paren {a + i b} } {2 i \paren {a^2 + b^2} } + C$$
Product of Complex Number with Conjugate
$$= \frac {a e^{a x} e^{i b x} - i b e^{a x} e^{i b x} - a e^{a x} e^{-i b x} - i b e^{a x} e^{-i b x} } {2 i \paren {a^2 + b^2} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {\frac {a e^{i b x} - i b e^{i b x} - a e^{-i b x} - i b e^{-i b x} } {2 i} } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {a \frac {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } {2 i} - b \frac {e^{i b x} + e^{-i b x} } 2 } + C$$
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {a \frac {e^{i b x} - e^{-i b x} } {2 i} - b \cos b x } + C$$
Cosine Exponential Formulation
$$= \frac {e^{a x} } {\paren {a^2 + b^2} } \paren {a \sin b x - b \cos b x } + C$$
Sine Exponential Formulation
$$= \frac {e^{a x} \paren {a \sin b x - b \cos b x} } {a^2 + b^2} + C$$

title: Primitive of Logarithm of x
theorem_text: $\ds \int \ln x \rd x = x \ln x - x + C$
proof_text:
Note that we have:
$$\int_0^1 \ln x \rd x = \int_0^1 x^0 \paren {\ln x}^1 \rd x$$
$$= \frac {\paren {-1}^1 \map \Gamma 2} {1^2}$$
Definite Integral from $0$ to $1$ of $x^m \paren {\ln x}^n$
$$= -1$$
Gamma Function Extends Factorial
We therefore have:
$$-1 = \int_0^1 \ln x \rd x$$
$$= \frac 1 a \int_0^a \map \ln {\frac u a} \rd u$$
substituting $x = \dfrac u a$ where $a > 0$
$$= \frac 1 a \int_0^a \paren {\ln u - \ln a} \rd u$$
Difference of Logarithms
$$= \frac 1 a \int_0^a \ln u \rd u - \ln a$$
Primitive of Constant, Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
giving:
$\displaystyle \frac 1 a \int_0^a \ln u \rd u = \ln a - 1$
so:
$\displaystyle \int_0^a \ln u \rd u = a \ln a - a$
for all real $a > 0$.
By Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: First Part, we have that:
$x \ln x - x$ is a primitive of $\ln x$ on $x > 0$.
We therefore conclude that, by Primitives which Differ by Constant:
$\displaystyle \int \ln x \rd x = x \ln x - x + C$
for $x > 0$.

title: Primitive of Hyperbolic Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \sinh a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\cosh a x} a + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \sinh a x \cosh a x \rd x = \int \frac {\sinh 2 a x} 2 \rd x$$
Double Angle Formula for Hyperbolic Sine
$$= \frac 1 2 \int \sinh 2 a x \rd x$$
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function
$$= \frac 1 2 \paren {\frac {\cosh 2 a x} {2 a} } + C$$
Primitive of $\sinh a x$
$$= \frac 1 2 \paren {\frac {1 + 2 \sinh^2 a x} {2 a} } + C$$
Corollary to Double Angle Formula for Hyperbolic Cosine
$$= \frac {\sinh^2 a x} {2 a} + \frac 1 {4 a} + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {\sinh^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
subsuming $\dfrac 1 {4 a}$ into arbitrary constant

title: Primitive of Hyperbolic Sine of a x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \sinh a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\cosh a x} a + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \sinh a x \cosh a x \rd x = \int \cosh a x \sinh a x \rd x$$
$$= \frac {\cosh^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
Primitive of $\cosh^n a x \sinh a x$ using $n = 1$
$$= \frac {1 + \sinh^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
Difference of Squares of Hyperbolic Cosine and Sine
$$= \frac 1 {2 a} + \frac {\sinh^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
simplifying
$$= \frac {\sinh^2 a x} {2 a} + C$$
subsuming $\dfrac 1 {2 a}$ into arbitrary constant

title: Primitive of Hyperbolic Cosine of a x over x
theorem_text:
$$\int \frac {\cosh a x \ \mathrm d x} x = \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac { \left({a x}\right)^{2 k} } {\left({2 k}\right) \left({2 k}\right)!} + C$$
$$= \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \frac {\left({a x}\right)^2} {2 \times 2!} + \frac {\left({a x}\right)^4} {4 \times 4!} + \frac {\left({a x}\right)^6} {6 \times 6!} + \cdots + C$$
proof_text:
$$\int \frac {\cosh a x \ \mathrm d x} x = \int \frac 1 x \left({\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\left({a x}\right)^{2 k} }{\left({2 k}\right)!} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Taylor Series Expansion for Hyperbolic Cosine Function
$$= \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {a^{2 k} } {\left({2 k}\right)!} \int \frac 1 x \left({x^{2 k} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
(1) $$= \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a^{2 k} } {\left({2 k}\right)!} \int \left({x^{2 k - 1} }\right) \ \mathrm d x$$
extracting case for $k = 0$
$$= \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a^{2 k} } {\left({2 k}\right)!} \frac {x^{2 k} } {2 k} + C$$
Primitive of Power
$$= \int \frac {\mathrm d x} x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\left({a x}\right)^{2 k} } {\left({2 k}\right) \left({2 k}\right)!} + C$$
simplifying
$$= \ln \left\vert{x}\right\vert + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\left({a x}\right)^{2 k} } {\left({2 k}\right) \left({2 k}\right)!} + C$$
Primitive of Reciprocal

title: Primitive of Hyperbolic Sine of a x by Hyperbolic Sine of p x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \sinh a x \sinh p x \rd x = \frac {\map \sinh {a + p} x} {2 \paren {a + p} } - \frac {\map \sinh {a - p} x} {2 \paren {a - p} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \sinh a x \sinh p x \rd x = \int \paren {\frac {\map \cosh {a x + p x} - \map \cosh {a x - p x} } 2} \rd x$$
Simpson's Formula for Hyperbolic Sine by Hyperbolic Sine
$$= \frac 1 2 \int \map \cosh {a + p} x \rd x - \frac 1 2 \int \map \cosh {a - p} x \rd x$$
Linear Combination of Integrals
$$= \frac 1 2 \frac {\map \sinh {a + p} x} {a + p} - \frac 1 2 \frac {\map \sinh {a - p} x} {a - p} + C$$
Primitive of $\cosh a x$
$$= \frac {\map \sinh {a + p} x} {2 \paren {a + p} } - \frac {\map \sinh {a - p} x} {2 \paren {a - p} } + C$$
simplifying

title: Primitive of Hyperbolic Cosine of a x by Hyperbolic Cosine of p x
theorem_text: $\displaystyle \int \cosh a x \cosh p x \rd x = \frac {\map \sinh {a + p} x} {2 \paren {a + p} } + \frac {\map \sinh {a - p} x} {2 \paren {a - p} } + C$
proof_text:
$$\int \cosh a x \cosh p x \rd x = \int \paren {\frac {\map \cosh {a x + p x} + \map \cosh {a x - p x} } 2} \rd x$$
Simpson's Formula for Hyperbolic Cosine by Hyperbolic Cosine
